items.title: Citrix NetScaler CVE-2026-88771: Observed Exploitation Artifacts and Hunt Indicators
items.description: CVE-2026-88771 is a critical pre-authentication command-injection vulnerability affecting Citrix NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway. LevelBlue's Threat Hunt Operations & Research (THOR) team identified active exploitation across multiple customer environments featuring malicious authentication events with attacker-controlled usernames containing pitboss and NSPPE strings. Observed activities included command-execution testing, payload retrieval using curl and wget, configuration collection and staging, reverse-shell deployment, persistence mechanisms, web-shell installation, and attempted exfiltration of NetScaler configuration data. Analysis revealed two second-stage payloads: main.py establishing reverse shells to command-and-control infrastructure, and update_c08937.pl creating privileged accounts, deploying PHP web shells, and attempting configuration exfiltration. Post-exploitation artifacts included creation of sec_monitor superuser accounts, modification of system binaries, deployment of .local_jou...

items.title: PaperCut MF Zero-Day Intrusion: Java Loader, Web Shell, and AdaptixC2 via CVE-2026-82078 and CVE-2026-81578
items.description: On August 31, 2026, threat actors exploited two zero-day vulnerabilities in PaperCut MF affecting a customer in the Education sector. The attackers targeted an internet-facing print server running vulnerable PaperCut MF version 24.0.2, deploying an in-memory Java loader that established a web shell. Through this web shell, they delivered a trojanized Microsoft Copilot binary containing an AdaptixC2 implant. The implant connected to command-and-control infrastructure hosted on Alibaba servers. After remaining dormant for approximately one day, attackers returned to perform reconnaissance and Active Directory enumeration. They then stole a token from a domain-privileged service account and moved laterally to a domain controller. On the compromised domain controller, they dumped credentials from memory and registry, enabled Windows Restricted Admin mode for pass-the-hash attacks, and extracted the NTDS.dit database containing password hashes for all domain accounts, achieving complete domain compromise.

items.title: Swarming Against Citrix 0-Day Exploitation
items.description: A malicious cyber actor exploited a Citrix NetScaler Gateway zero-day vulnerability on September 24, 2026, three days before public disclosure. The attacker, using IP address 149.104.78.141, attempted exploitation that was detected through behavioral analysis despite no CVE-specific signatures existing at the time. The exploitation chain aimed to establish persistence through a password-protected webshell, attempting to set setuid and setgid bits on /bin/sh for root access. The attacker tried to configure the web server to execute a hidden PHP webshell disguised as a CSS file, using aliases to route requests. Though unsuccessful in compromising the targeted sensor, the post-exploitation playbook revealed sophisticated techniques for maintaining access and evading detection through web server manipulation.

items.title: Star Blizzard refines phishing and malware delivery with the RedFlick technique
items.description: Since January 2026, Microsoft has observed Russian state threat actor Star Blizzard evolve their detection evasion capabilities through large-scale phishing campaigns, the use of accounts on compromised websites, and a novel malware delivery technique that Microsoft tracks as “RedFlick”. These changes represent a notable shift in the actor’s operational tradecraft and support ongoing cyberespionage activity targeting Ukrainian individuals and institutions as well as international non-government organizations (NGOs), Western think tanks, governments, and other organizations associated with international policy—particularly those with a nexus in supporting Ukraine.

items.title: 2CLoader: A New Malware Loader Delivering Vidar and Remus
items.description: In August 2026, a new loader designated 2CLoader was identified being used to distribute information stealers including Vidar and Remus, along with XWorm RAT. The loader implements extensive anti-analysis capabilities including anti-VM, anti-debug, and user activity checks. It employs sophisticated evasion techniques such as indirect system calls using Hell's Gate technique and inline trampoline hooks to bypass endpoint security detection. The loader stores its configuration and encrypted payload as a PE resource, using rolling XOR and AES-GCM encryption for payload protection. It supports multiple payload execution methods including RunPE, LoadPE, and CLR hosting for .NET assemblies. Network communication with command-and-control servers uses HTTP POST requests with JSON formatted messages encrypted via XOR. Multiple persistence mechanisms are available through registry keys, scheduled tasks, and startup folders.

items.title: Unauthenticated command injection on internet-facing mail servers: tracking CVE-2026-73570
items.description: Microsoft Threat Intelligence identified active exploitation of CVE-2026-73570, an unauthenticated OS command injection vulnerability in Zimbra Collaboration Suite's SNMP notification path. Exploitation occurred between patch availability on July 20, 2026 and public disclosure on August 13, 2026. Attackers delivered JSP webshells and reverse shells without requiring authentication, achieving privilege escalation through PAM configuration abuse and establishing persistent access via systemd services. Post-exploitation activity included cluster-wide lateral movement using Zimbra SSH keys, collection of authentication secrets and mailbox data, and attempted exfiltration using cloud-storage tools. Multiple organizations across different regions and industries were affected through both automated payload delivery and hands-on-keyboard operations targeting internet-facing Zimbra mail servers.

items.title: Inside Coruna and DarkSword Chains: From Web Lures to iOS Exploitation
items.description: Seven months after initial disclosure, the Coruna iOS exploit framework continues to evolve, now deploying two distinct chains based on device operating system version. Targets running iOS 17.2.1 or earlier receive the legacy Coruna framework, while later builds receive DarkSword-derived chains. Analysis identified 608 domains delivering Coruna-family code, with 93 sites mapping to 21 distinct tracking collectors. Distribution spans dating portals, AI-companion platforms, cryptocurrency promotions, media streaming services, and compromised legitimate sites. The attack requires no user interaction beyond loading a webpage, operating through hidden iframes that deploy browser exploits leading to native code execution. Recovered modules include kernel memory manipulation, code-signing enforcement changes, process memory access, encrypted command-and-control communication, and cleanup routines. One delivery vector involves compromised npm packages, enabling legitimate websites to serve exploits through their o...

items.title: Kairos Hold'em: Dissecting a New Go-Based DDoS Botnet
items.description: Kairos is a newly documented DDoS botnet for Linux written in Go, designed to transform compromised machines into attack nodes. The bot establishes hundreds to thousands of TCP connections to operator-specified targets, maintaining them with minimal keepalive bytes every few seconds to exhaust victim services. Initial access occurs via Telnet using default root credentials with empty passwords. The payload is delivered through multi-fallback shell commands via HTTP from the same server used for command and control. The bot operates with a simple three-command protocol including hold, kill all, and kill unpause commands. It masquerades as a kernel worker thread and employs a build-per-C2 distribution model, with samples identified across multiple CPU architectures including x86_64, ARM, MIPS, and 386.

items.title: Trojanized Claude Code Extension Plants an SSH Backdoor
items.description: Version 2.1.313 of the Claude Code extension in the Cursor Marketplace was compromised on October 29th, 2026. A malicious 66-line loader was inserted before legitimate extension code in the extension.js file. Upon activation, it adds an attacker-controlled SSH key labeled 'svc-telemetry' to the victim's authorized_keys, attempts to enable local SSH services, and establishes a reverse SSH tunnel to 134.209.82.225. The implant collects reconnaissance data including hostname, user information, Git configuration, and environment variables containing credentials. It installs platform-specific persistence mechanisms using LaunchAgents on macOS, crontab on Linux, and scheduled tasks on Windows. Beacon data is transmitted unencrypted to the command-and-control infrastructure, providing persistent remote access through the established SSH tunnel.

items.title: Polymarket Breach Alert: Wallet-Draining Code Found in a Third-Party Script
items.description: A malicious JavaScript file was discovered in a third-party performance monitoring integration on Polymarket. The script, hosted on a DebugBear CDN URL, contained sophisticated code designed to access authenticated trading sessions, inspect user portfolios, and transfer cryptocurrency assets to attacker-controlled addresses. The payload searches for active trading clients and signers within the user's browser session, then attempts to sell positions or transfer tokens directly. Analysis revealed code that reads authentication context from local storage, traverses React component structures to locate trading functionality, and constructs EIP-712 signed messages to move assets. A fallback recipient address embedded in the script showed holdings exceeding $2.1 million. Production build metadata from Polymarket confirms removal of the DebugBear integration. While the script's malicious capabilities are established through static analysis, the total number of victims and aggregate losses remain unverified.

items.title: How Attackers Redirect Crypto Payments
items.description: Cryptocurrency transactions face unique threats from specialized malware known as Clipbankers, designed to redirect payments by replacing copied wallet addresses with attacker-controlled ones. These attacks exploit user trust in clipboard functions, the difficulty of memorizing long cryptographic strings, and the irreversible nature of blockchain transactions. Two prominent families, AnimateClipper and Efimer, demonstrate sophisticated capabilities including pattern matching and digit-matching techniques to minimize detection. AnimateClipper emerged in January 2026 and monitors clipboards for cryptocurrency patterns across multiple networks. Efimer employs advanced evasion techniques including Pyarmor protection, XOR encryption, and TOR-based command and control communications, while matching leading or trailing digits of addresses. Both families are distributed through social engineering methods including ClickFix campaigns, phishing emails, and fake software installations. The malware families became lar...

items.title: Prediction Markets Emerge as a New Vertical for Traffer Teams
items.description: Multiple Russian-language traffer teams have rapidly adapted affiliate-fraud models to exploit growing interest in prediction markets like PolyMarket and Kalshi since spring 2026. Three teams—AtlasCore, PolyFucked, and Magnetic Team—provide comprehensive fraud infrastructure including websites, administrative panels, cryptocurrency payment systems, and technical support. These services enable affiliates to deploy convincing prediction-market interfaces combined with established fraud mechanisms such as controlled trading outcomes, fabricated market activity, artificial withdrawal restrictions, and collection of sensitive identity information. Artificial intelligence accelerates these operations by reducing time and expertise required for platform development, content creation, social engineering, and victim engagement. The rapid adoption demonstrates how mature fraud ecosystems can pivot toward emerging technologies and financial products without developing entirely new criminal capabilities. Prediction ma...

items.title: Aurora ransomware targets ESXi abuses Cursor Agent for exploitation
items.description: Aurora ransomware group has been active since approximately April 2026, targeting organizations across multiple countries and operating a data leak site. The investigation revealed the group deploys a Linux ransomware variant specifically designed for ESXi environments, using ChaCha20 encryption with RSA-4096 key wrapping. A distinctive characteristic includes the abuse of Cursor Agent with Claude Sonnet AI to assist with hands-on exploitation activities across ten target organizations between April and May 2026. The AI agent performed tasks including privilege enumeration, network scanning, NTLM relay attacks, and certificate attacks. Operators imposed specific restrictions prohibiting DCSync, account lockouts, and adding new computer objects to domains. A second cluster of activity attributed to Aurora used different tactics including SQL Server lateral movement, GodPotato escalation, and S3-based exfiltration affecting eight organizations across multiple countries.

items.title: SEO Poisoning Campaign Targets DeepSeek Users: Chinese Threat Actor Deploys Kong RAT via Multi-Stage Attacks
items.description: A sophisticated SEO poisoning campaign targets users searching for DeepSeek AI tools through malicious lookalike domains positioned on first-page search results. The attack employs a multi-stage infection chain beginning with weaponized MSI files disguised as legitimate DeepSeek software. The execution flow progresses through multiple stages involving shellcode, DLL side-loading via legitimate Cyglaunch software, and ultimately deploys Kong RAT. The threat actor registered domains mimicking DeepSeek and distributed ZIP archives containing code-signed fake installers to add legitimacy. Attribution points to a potential Chinese threat actor based on PDB paths referencing '52pojie', a Chinese cybersecurity forum. This campaign appears to be a continuation of previous operations from April 2026 targeting users of Chinese developer tools including FinalShell SSH client, Xshell, and Clash proxy. The final payload includes keylogger functionality and establishes persistence through registry modifications.

items.title: Node2Shell (CVE-2026-111497): Brotli RCE Exploited
items.description: A critical out-of-bounds write vulnerability in Google's Brotli decompression library allows specially crafted compressed data to corrupt application memory, potentially enabling remote code execution. The flaw, scoring 9.2 CVSS v4.0, affects Google Brotli versions 1.0.3 through 1.2.0 and impacts multiple platforms including Node.js, Bun, Python implementations, and .NET frameworks. Exploitation attempts were observed within days of patch availability, with working proof-of-concept code demonstrating remote code execution against Node.js environments through malicious HTTP requests and responses. CISA added the vulnerability to its KEV catalog on October 27, 2026. The vulnerability can be triggered through various attack vectors including incoming HTTP requests with Brotli-compressed bodies, malicious server responses, and file processing workflows. Enterprise products from Palo Alto Networks and VMware are also affected, expanding the attack surface beyond typical Node.js deployments.

items.title: Investigating Abuse of Remote Desktop and Bulk Mailing Apps
items.description: Investigation into a tech-support scam led to discovering connections between the remote-access application UltraViewer and bulk-mailing software UltraMailer. DNS and email analysis revealed a long-running QuickBooks phishing campaign utilizing over 350 lookalike domains and tracking domain chanret[.]com. The campaign directs victims to call scammers attempting to steal QuickBooks credentials while exposing recipient information through UltraMailer tracking pixels. UltraMailer is openly promoted on criminal forums as a spamming tool with no abuse-reporting mechanism. The investigation also uncovered trojanized installers containing authentic copies of both applications, including one UltraMailer installer carrying njRAT. When the QuickBooks actor briefly switched to Mail250, the account was suspended after reporting, but the campaign resumed using UltraMailer infrastructure. While no evidence suggests developers participated in these activities, the findings demonstrate widespread criminal abuse of legitim...

items.title: MadApe: The Code That Opens the Door
items.description: A previously undocumented Microsoft Device Code phishing kit named MadApe has been uncovered, operating through a multi-stage campaign that combines business-themed PDF lures, configurable redirect chains, and fake document-sharing pages. The kit abuses Microsoft's legitimate Device Code authentication flow to gain access to victim accounts without collecting credentials on phishing pages. The campaign demonstrates sophisticated infrastructure comprising 155 root domains registered between June and August 2026, primarily through Dynadot. Multiple phishing templates impersonate SharePoint, OneDrive, Teams, Adobe Acrobat, and DocuSign while sharing identical backend functionality. The infrastructure includes custom human-verification challenges, decoy websites using shared templates, and operator panels exposed on the same hosts serving phishing pages. The activity shows broad localization across at least nine languages and targets business-related communications.

items.title: Sandbox Flipped to 'Danger-Full-Access': Unauthorized AI Relays Create Risk for Organizations
items.description: An unauthorized relay service has been installing genuine OpenAI Codex and Anthropic Claude Code command-line interfaces on enterprise systems, then reconfiguring them to route all requests through third-party infrastructure. Active since early 2026, the service has impacted organizations primarily in mainland China, with additional cases in South Korea, Taiwan, and Malaysia. Affected sectors include industrial automation, electronics manufacturing, semiconductors, pharmaceuticals, and petrochemicals. The delivery mechanism uses fileless PowerShell or bash scripts fetched from lookalike domains. The reconfiguration disables execution sandboxes entirely, enables network access, replaces legitimate API credentials with relay-issued tokens, and disables telemetry. While no evidence of abuse exists, the configuration grants operators access to read every prompt, file, and secret, with commands executing under full user privileges.

items.title: NIK C2: The new AI-enabled command-and-control framework
items.description: A sophisticated AI-integrated command-and-control framework named NIK C2 has been discovered, featuring a Windows implant capable of credential dumping, keystroke streaming, and real-time AI-powered data analysis through the OpenAI Chat Completions API. The Go-based implant employs dual-channel C2 architecture with TLS-secured WebSockets and HTTP fallback, utilizing AES-256-GCM encryption. It includes surveillance capabilities, lateral movement tools, screen-locking ransomware deployment demanding Bitcoin or USDT payment, and bootkit preparation features. The framework demonstrates advanced defense evasion through AMSI patching, process hollowing, and anti-debugging measures. Development spans at least three versions compiled with Go 1.23.4, indicating active evolution by a technically proficient team. Active C2 infrastructure was observed at IP 87.120.196[.]120 hosting domain total-sitevv[.]lol, confirming operational deployment beyond proof-of-concept status.

items.title: Fake "View & Sign" and Adobe Acrobat Lures Deliver Attacker-Configured ScreenConnect Clients
items.description: Researchers uncovered fake Adobe Acrobat and "View & Sign" pages distributing legitimate, digitally signed ConnectWise ScreenConnect installers configured for unauthorized remote access. The campaign uses Telegram bots to track visitors, profile devices and networks, and automatically download remote-access clients when specific criteria are met. Five distinct page variants share near-identical JavaScript and common background images, applying operating-system and ISP-based checks before delivery. The installers connect to separate ScreenConnect Cloud tenants including omydze, vvvzou, luminahealthturkey2, tfcconnection, and alunos1. If executed, these clients establish persistent remote access running as LocalSystem. The threat weaponizes trusted software with valid digital signatures to bypass traditional security controls, requiring defenders to focus on identifying unauthorized tenant configurations rather than relying solely on file hashes.

items.title: Unknown APT uses NetamLoader to attack a Win10 OS customized for governments in Asia
items.description: A sophisticated supply-chain attack has been discovered targeting a custom Windows 10 build used exclusively by government entities in Asia. The attack employs a complex multi-stage infection chain called NetamLoader, leveraging XAML markup and .NET assemblies. The malicious framework begins with a CAB archive placed in Windows update directories, exploiting AppDomainManager injection and BinaryFormatter deserialization vulnerabilities. The attack chain progresses through multiple stages involving XAML loaders, bypasses AMSI protection, and deploys a plugin that communicates with command-and-control infrastructure. The framework uses AES encryption for network traffic, implements anti-analysis techniques including 22-28 hour polling intervals, and removes forensic evidence. The malware operates covertly by migrating to dllhost.exe and uses isolated AppDomains for payload execution. Commercial hosting infrastructure including Cloudflare CDN was utilized.

items.title: Adversary Unmasked APT Profile - Star Blizzard
items.description: Star Blizzard, attributed to the Russian Federal Security Service Centre 18, is a persistent espionage group targeting government officials, defence personnel, think tanks, NGOs, and academia primarily in the UK, US, Ukraine, and NATO countries. The group conducts credential theft and hack-and-leak operations through sophisticated spear-phishing, impersonation, and relationship building. Since 2024, operations expanded from credential harvesting to deploying endpoint malware including SPICA, YESROBOT, MAYBEROBOT, and CosmicPulse backdoors. Notable shifts include moving from targeted to bulk phishing campaigns, incorporating fake CAPTCHA lures, exploiting iOS devices with leaked DarkSword exploit kit, and using compromised WordPress sites as infrastructure. The group rapidly adapts tooling after exposure, with new malware variants appearing within days of public disclosure. Recent campaigns targeted over 100 organizations using the RedFlick delivery chain, demonstrating increased scale and sophistication.

items.title: PHP2Shell: Exploitation Attempts and Remediation Trends
items.description: Wiz Research has been monitoring exploitation attempts targeting two critical PHP vulnerabilities since their public disclosure on October 21, 2026. While no successful attacks have been observed in their telemetry, some private exploits have been shared that work against various targets. Telemetry shows a 67% decrease in exposed vulnerable machines and a 47.9% reduction in significantly affected organizations within one week. Observed exploitation attempts include tools using the PHP2Shell mechanism matching public proof-of-concepts, though none completed the full exploit chain. Challenges preventing successful exploitation include request-size limits, memory exhaustion failures, and difficulties with worker pinning across different PHP configurations. Additionally, some tools branded as PHP2Shell exploits actually relied on unrelated session poisoning techniques requiring separate local file inclusion vulnerabilities. Despite limited success to date, PHP2Shell remains a significant risk requiring immedia...

items.title: Attackers Abuse ChatGPT Custom GPTs to Deliver RAT via ClickFix
items.description: Threat actors are exploiting ChatGPT Custom GPTs and Google Sites to deliver remote access trojans through a sophisticated multi-stage attack chain. The campaign uses sponsored Google search results to direct victims to attacker-created Custom GPTs that impersonate legitimate ChatGPT models. Victims are then redirected to a malicious Google Sites page presenting a fake CloudFlare CAPTCHA that deploys a ClickFix lure, tricking users into executing PowerShell commands. This initiates an eight-stage infection chain involving obfuscated scripts, malicious MSI installers, and DLL sideloading through legitimately signed Canon or Stardock executables. The payload establishes dual persistence mechanisms and deploys a full-featured RAT with capabilities including remote desktop access, credential harvesting from seventeen browsers, file management, and payload deployment. Huntress investigators responded to at least 40 related incidents with two confirmed Custom GPT-driven infections.

items.title: Node2Shell / HTTP2Shell Vulnerability May Allow RCE
items.description: An out-of-bounds write vulnerability in Google's Brotli decoder, tracked as CVE-2026-111497 and known as Node2Shell or HTTP2Shell, affects Node.js and various other software packages. The critical flaw (CVSS 9.2) can be triggered when vulnerable processes decompress attacker-controlled Brotli data, potentially leading to crashes, memory disclosure, or remote code execution. The vulnerability impacts multiple runtimes including Node.js, Bun, Python, .NET, Envoy Proxy, and Java brotli4j. Exploitation can occur through both inbound malicious requests and outbound responses from compromised servers. Within 24 hours of disclosure, reconnaissance and exploitation attempts were observed from 20 source IP addresses across 402 events, with 40% involving reconnaissance and 60% exploitation attempts. Organizations should immediately patch vulnerable components and monitor for suspicious activity.

items.title: n0n Ransomware: Inside an AI-Assisted Extortion Operation
items.description: In September 2026, an exposed staging server revealed the complete operational workspace of a n0n ransomware operator, including breach tools, encryptor source code, extortion infrastructure, and an AI coding agent environment with over $7,000 in paid LLM API usage. The investigation identified at least 23 victim organizations across 14 countries spanning multiple sectors. Every documented compromise relied exclusively on weak or stolen credentials, with no vulnerability exploitation observed. The operation combines data exfiltration with either encryption or complete data destruction, including backup deletion. The operator leveraged an AI coding agent configured with 154 models to generate hundreds of attack scripts, demonstrating human-directed operations augmented by artificial intelligence. By October 2026, n0n had listed 93 victims with combined ransom demands totaling $283.7 million, using credential stuffing against FortiGate SSL-VPN devices, exposed cloud keys, and compromised management portals a...

items.title: PHP2Shell Weaponized After Japanese Real Estate Extortion
items.description: An exposed staging server at 96.126.130.81 revealed an operator's extortion campaign targeting Japanese real estate websites between October 9-11, 2026, followed by PHP2Shell exploitation tooling. The operator, using the handle kkkkevin777, compromised one Japanese real estate services company and pivoted to nearly 20 related sites through shared hosting credentials. Stolen data included 16,061 customer records with plaintext passwords, income details, and addresses. The operator deployed ransom pages with an October 11 deadline and pressured victims by threatening to expose customer data. PHP2Shell tooling arrived on October 21, ten days after the extortion wave, indicating the operator was preparing new capabilities. Additionally, databases and emails from a Taiwanese company were exfiltrated. The server contained weaponized PHP2Shell reproducers, web shells, beacon logs, and scripts for lateral movement, though no confirmed PHP2Shell exploitation against live targets was documented.

items.title: 68 GB Stolen From a Philippine Government Agency's Overseas-Employment Databases, Exposed by the Operator's Own Open Directory
items.description: An unidentified operator exfiltrated 68.837 GiB of database backups from a Philippine government agency managing overseas employment and migrant workers on 6 September 2026. The theft involved 27 SQL Server backups containing case-management systems including POEA and OFW variants. The operator inadvertently exposed their staging infrastructure via an open HTTP directory on a UpCloud VPS in Singapore, revealing a rebranded GodPotato privilege escalation tool (renamed Wrqsnx), PowerShell stagers, Impacket toolkit, and transfer logs. The payload leverages DCOM and RPC mechanisms to achieve SYSTEM-level access without exploiting vulnerabilities. Certificate analysis linked the compromised infrastructure to the Philippine Overseas Employment Administration portal farm. Initial access vectors and command-and-control channels remain unidentified, though tooling was delivered to agency portal hosts.

items.title: Managed for Malice: How Attackers Turn MDM into Remote Access
items.description: Threat actors are weaponizing legitimate mobile device management platforms, including Hexnode and Rippling, through social engineering techniques to establish unauthorized remote access to victim systems. Attackers use phishing emails with business-themed lures, such as proposals and meeting invitations, to trick users into enrolling devices or installing management agents. Once MDM access is established, adversaries leverage this trusted, privileged path to deploy unauthorized remote monitoring and management tools like ScreenConnect, which connect to attacker-controlled relays. The deployment chain typically follows a pattern: social engineering leading to MDM enrollment, followed by RMM installation and external relay connections. This technique demonstrates the challenge of distinguishing legitimate administrative tools from malicious use, as the MDM platforms themselves are not compromised but rather misused through deception.

items.title: False Protection, Emptied Accounts: The Seven Android Trojan Families Targeting Indian Banking Apps
items.description: Group-IB's Threat Intelligence team uncovered a sophisticated Android malware campaign systematically targeting India's financial services sector since July 2025, orchestrated by the financially-motivated threat cluster CyberDakait. The operation distributes seven distinct malware families through coordinated smishing and vishing campaigns, impersonating bank representatives to trick victims into installing malicious APKs. These trojans harvest sensitive banking credentials, credit card details, and outstanding balances through overlay attacks while simultaneously conducting cryptojacking using XMRig. The malicious applications are hosted on GitHub repositories to maintain legitimacy, with the initial APK functioning as a dropper for the main payload and cryptocurrency mining module. Analysis revealed at least 17,960 compromised devices with 7.6 million intercepted SMS messages, including OTPs and transaction notifications. items.title: Amazon Threat Intelligence identifies PHP2Shell exploitation prior to public disclosure in MadPot
items.description: Amazon Threat Intelligence discovered PHP2Shell exploitation attempts in MadPot honeypot telemetry on October 17, 2026, four days before the public disclosure of CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619. The initial exploit originated from a commercial anonymization network, suggesting threat actor involvement during the embargo period. Multiple proof-of-concept exploits emerged on the disclosure date, with varied payloads and infrastructure indicating multiple actors. Following the embargo lift on October 21, 2026, exploitation became widespread within hours. This incident highlights two critical lessons: coordinated disclosure cannot guarantee zero-day protection, and AI-assisted analysis has dramatically shortened the time from patch release to working exploits, requiring organizations to measure patch timelines in hours rather than days.

items.title: Telerik UI Exploitation Leads to Webshell Install and Scanner Execution
items.description: Multiple attack campaigns exploiting CVE-2019-18935, a remote code execution vulnerability in unpatched Telerik UI for ASP.NET AJAX servers, have been identified. The first case involved exploiting the vulnerability to execute a reverse shell connecting to 206.82.6.22, attempting privilege escalation using Potato-family tools like SweetPotato, and installing a Godzilla-style memory-based web shell that operates within the w3wp.exe process without requiring separate ASPX files. The second case deployed a Rust-based scanner tool that searches for exposed WordPress installation pages across target systems and reports findings via Telegram. Both attacks targeted Windows IIS servers, enabling attackers to maintain persistent access, collect system information, and identify additional targets for future campaigns.

items.title: Inside "MR ROBOT" - Anatomy of a Malware-as-a-Service Operation Targeting Indian Bank Customers
items.description: A sophisticated Android Malware-as-a-Service operation called MR ROBOT is actively targeting Indian bank customers through a subscription-based model. The platform enables cybercriminals to rent customized banking trojans distributed via fake Play Store pages and messaging apps. The operation uses a multi-stage dropper that decrypts encrypted payloads to deploy banking trojans capable of intercepting SMS and OTPs, silently enabling call forwarding using the *21# carrier code to bypass phone-based two-factor authentication, and overlaying phishing screens to harvest card details, CVV, ATM PINs, UPI credentials, and identity documents. One tracked affiliate compromised 153 devices and intercepted 5,407 SMS messages across multiple Indian banks. The operation features a Telegram bot storefront offering approximately 36 fake applications impersonating banks, utility providers, and government services, with stolen data exfiltrated to Firebase Realtime Database and Telegram channels.

items.title: Malicious Firefox Extensions Impersonate Phantom, Jupiter, and Bitget to Steal Wallet Secrets
items.description: Three malicious Firefox extensions impersonating popular cryptocurrency wallets—Phantom, Jupiter, and Bitget—were discovered stealing recovery phrases and private keys from users. The extensions use Unicode homoglyphs to mimic legitimate wallet names and route stolen credentials to brand-named subdomains of bonto[.]io. The Phantom impersonator employs a two-stage approach: a loader fetches additional payloads from a remote server at runtime, allowing operators to modify malicious code post-review. All three extensions bundle complete stealers in signed packages that capture seed phrases, private keys, and clipboard data. The campaign uses separate throwaway developer accounts for each listing and provisions infrastructure for additional targets including Coinbase and Exodus wallets. Captured secrets grant attackers complete control over victims' cryptocurrency wallets and assets.

items.title: September 2026 Infostealer Trend Report
items.description: During September 2026, infostealers were primarily distributed through SEO poisoning, disguised as illegal software such as cracks and keygens. Major distribution platforms included Mediafire, AWS S3, Mega, and Cloudflare Storage. EXE files comprised 90.8% of samples, while DLL side-loading accounted for 9.2%, utilizing legitimate files like python37.dll and POWRPROF.dll. A new infostealer named Lzveil, built with Rust, downloads configuration data from C2 servers and uses modified Base64 decryption, XOR encryption, and LZNT1 compression. Email campaigns distributed DarkCloud and AgentTesla infostealers, impersonating construction and logistics companies respectively. Both steal credentials, browser data, cryptocurrency wallets, and system information. The stolen data is often traded on dark web markets or used for secondary attacks.

items.title: Inside Qilin ransomware: ESXi attacks, affiliate networks and double extortion
items.description: Qilin, also known as Agenda, is a Russian-speaking ransomware-as-a-service operation active since 2022 that became one of the most prolific groups by 2025 with over 1,000 claimed victims. The operation employs a flexible platform allowing affiliates to customize attacks targeting local files, network shares, and virtual machine infrastructure. Affiliates typically gain initial access through phishing, stolen credentials, vulnerable internet-facing systems, and remote management tools. The group follows a double-extortion model, encrypting systems while threatening to publish stolen data via their blog and WikiLeaksV2 platform. Notable incidents include the 2024 Synnovis attack affecting UK healthcare services. Qilin has been linked to Moonstone Sleet and Scattered Spider, with some operators creating derivative operations including The Gentlemen and Securotrop, the latter maintaining affiliate status while operating an independent leak site.

items.title: RATatouille: Today's Special: Impersonating Companies in Korea, Payments in Cryptocurrency
items.description: Infrastructure tracking related to ValleyRAT led to the discovery of multiple fraudulent websites impersonating legitimate Korean companies including Doosan Robotics and Cheonjeong. These sites used authentic corporate logos, videos, and descriptions to appear legitimate while offering features like invitation-code registration, VIP memberships, and cryptocurrency deposit/withdrawal functions. Online chat support provided instructions for USDT payments via TRON wallet addresses, requiring users to submit transaction screenshots. Analysis revealed TRON wallet addresses with significant transaction volumes, including one wallet that received approximately 13 million USDT cumulatively. Infrastructure analysis starting from ValleyRAT C2 IP address 14.128.53[.]155 identified 12 potentially associated domains. However, no direct operational connection has been confirmed between ValleyRAT malware operations and these fraudulent websites or cryptocurrency wallets.

items.title: Omegatech Is Disrupted, and the Pressure on Bulletproof Hosting Keeps Building
items.description: The FBI seized virtualine[.]net on October 27, 2026, under Operation Omegaline, targeting Virtualine Technologies, which operated as Omegatech (AS202412). This bulletproof hosting provider emerged in February 2026 after infrastructure shifted from Railnet LLC (AS214943). Bulletproof hosting providers rent servers to cybercriminals while ignoring abuse complaints, enabling phishing, malware, and ransomware operations. Over the past year, 50 such providers lost their autonomous system numbers due to law enforcement action, sanctions, or strategic abandonment. Despite seizures, operators quickly rebrand and acquire new ASNs within days, moving malicious IP ranges to continue operations. Recent enforcement actions include Dutch seizure of THE.Hosting servers, US charges against Russian nationals, and EU sanctions against Media Land. The investigation involved FBI Washington Field Office, Germany's Polizei Hessen, Netherlands' Politie Midden-Nederland, UK's National Crime Agency, and private partners.

items.title: Operation Master: Deconstructing a Multi-Tiered Intrusion and Monetization Pipeline
items.description: A sophisticated cybercrime operation compromised enterprise networks across multiple countries by exploiting a GlobalProtect authentication bypass vulnerability (CVE-2026-0257), executed advanced web application attacks, and deployed the AdaptixC2 framework. The operation scanned 277.5 million addresses to curate 81 high-value targets, stole databases from 9+ instances via SQL injection with xp_cmdshell escalation, and exfiltrated Active Directory credentials. Monetization occurred through dual strategies: initially selling corporate and energy sector databases on underground forums under the persona "masterblack", then weaponizing the same data to power a multi-tenant automated invoice fraud platform generating 2.4 million phishing messages and 622,666 personalized fraudulent links. The infrastructure utilized domainless phishing tactics including M365 OAuth device-code phishing and voice-based credential harvesting, collecting payments via PIX through serverless proxies. The operation was exposed in mid-...

items.title: SkyW4lker Phishing Kit: Microsoft 365 Threat to US Firms
items.description: SkyW4lker is an active device-code phishing kit exploiting Microsoft 365 authentication processes across the United States, Europe, and other regions. Operating since June 2026, it bypasses MFA by abusing legitimate OAuth 2.0 device-code flows, granting attackers access to corporate accounts without stealing passwords. The kit uses phishing emails with password-protected attachments containing links that lead victims through CAPTCHA pages to malicious sites requesting Microsoft device codes. Analysis revealed 618 sandbox submissions between June and October 2026, with 46% originating from US organizations. Monthly activity surged from 20 cases in June to 200 in September. Technical investigation uncovered shared infrastructure and code similarities with the Gabagool credential phishing kit, suggesting common development. The kit employs obfuscated JavaScript, IP-based geolocation, and PHP backends to track victim authentication status, primarily targeting technology, manufacturing, and government sectors.

items.title: Automated Subversion and Attempted Takeover of AI Pentesting Harnesses
items.description: Unprotected Cairn AI intrusion harnesses are being systematically compromised by unknown actors through automated campaigns that began around October 20, 2026. Attackers insert malicious tasks that manipulate agents to compromise the host systems, involving profiling installations, stealing secrets including AI model API keys, downloading Poseidon malware, and installing unauthorized SSH keys. Two distinct threat clusters, designated AIA0009 and AIA0010, conduct synchronized waves of attacks across multiple panels. AIA0009 focuses on persistence and malware deployment, while AIA0010 emphasizes exploration and credential extraction. The campaigns appear highly automated and possibly agentic, utilizing AI to attack AI operations. Activities include container escape attempts, reconnaissance of host environments, and deployment of Poseidon RAT configured with Bunny.net CDN command and control infrastructure.

items.title: Locked and Loaded: Phishing through Fake Bids and Protected Documents
items.description: A sophisticated credential phishing campaign leverages fake business bid invitations to target professionals. The attack begins with an email titled 'Project Bid Invitation' containing a password-protected PDF attachment that evades automated security scanning. Once opened, the PDF displays a fake OneDrive button redirecting victims to a fraudulent shared document drive. Recipients are prompted to select files for download, then asked to enter their email address, mimicking legitimate document-sharing platforms. This leads to a counterfeit Microsoft login page where entered credentials are harvested and transmitted to attacker-controlled servers. The campaign exploits trusted business processes, password protection mechanisms, and familiar brand interfaces to bypass both technical defenses and human vigilance, making it particularly effective against employees conditioned to respond urgently to legitimate business opportunities.

items.title: Notorious Brazilian Magecart group hijacks Convertr checkouts via Plausible analytics
items.description: A Brazilian Magecart group, active since 2024, conducted a supply chain attack by injecting a card skimmer into the Plausible analytics script of Brazilian ecommerce platform Convertr. Starting October 24, 2026, all Convertr checkouts loaded the malicious tracker from analytics.convertr.app.br, stealing card details, CVV, expiry dates, cardholder names, and CPF taxpayer numbers from shoppers. The stolen data was exfiltrated to 1x0.is. The attackers exploited CVE-2026-8467, a critical vulnerability in Plausible Community Edition versions 3.0.0 through 3.2.0, which allowed command execution through an exposed component. Convertr removed the skimmer and patched Plausible on October 27. This group has targeted dozens of Brazilian stores running Magento, OpenCart, and WooCommerce since 2024, using distinctive techniques including pipe-delimited data exfiltration and Portuguese-named endpoints.

items.title: Camera Management Software Compromise Leads to Malware Deployment
items.description: Attackers compromised camera management software (CMS.exe) to gain initial access to multiple organizational environments. Following compromise, adversaries deployed rs.win32.exe into user AppData directories and leveraged DLL sideloading by placing the legitimate Windows binary WpcMon.exe alongside malicious DLLs (IPHLPAPI.DLL and samcli.dll) in non-standard locations. These modified DLLs, based on zlib compression libraries, incorporated beaconing functionality to communicate with a command-and-control server at 144.172.116.37. Persistence was established through Run Key registry modifications. The camera management software, potentially linked to 3R Global and kvision.ai, lacked adequate security controls and logging capabilities. Organizations should treat camera systems and their management platforms as critical components of the enterprise attack surface, implementing proper access controls, monitoring unusual process chains, and restricting executable execution in user-writable paths.

items.title: Inside ICMacOS: From an Infostealer to a Persistent RAT
items.description: ICMacOS (Icarus macOS) is a newly identified macOS Malware-as-a-Service stealer actively marketed since September 2026 by the Russian-speaking actor GlowComa on underground forums. The malware targets macOS systems running Sierra through current versions on both Intel and Apple Silicon architectures. Initially designed as a credential stealer, it rapidly evolved into a persistent remote access trojan with WebSocket-based command-and-control capabilities. The infection chain uses ClickFix social engineering to deliver dropper scripts that harvest administrator passwords through fake system dialogs before deploying the primary payload. Version 1 focuses on stealing browser credentials, cryptocurrency wallets, developer secrets, messaging data, and password managers. Version 2 introduces full RAT functionality with LaunchAgent persistence and interactive shell access while expanding data collection to include Steam accounts, Outlook data, and additional password managers.

items.title: Domain Shadowing: Attackers Abuse Institutional Domains
items.description: Two unrelated operations exploited domain shadowing techniques to place illegal gambling content beneath legitimate educational and government domains in Bangladesh, India, and Mexico. Unauthorized parties gained access to DNS administration, creating records beneath established institutional namespaces to leverage their reputation for search engine optimization. Hidden Hawk added individual CNAME records mapping institutional hostnames to gambling pages hosted primarily on Cloudflare Pages, affecting over 850 entry points across eight domains. A separate campaign targeting Maharashtra government domains delegated entire subzones to third-party nameservers using wildcards, enabling external management of numerous hostnames. Both operations served Indonesian and Indian illegal gambling content worth an estimated $6 trillion globally in unregulated markets, exploiting institutional trust to boost search rankings and acquire traffic while leaving primary websites intact and potentially unnoticed by domain own...

items.title: Tricks from the Past deployed via signed ChatGPT and Claude binaries
items.description: Check Point Research discovered a campaign tracked as Yoba that exploits the popularity of AI tools like ChatGPT and Claude. Attackers created fake GitHub projects mimicking desktop applications such as GPT-5.6 Sol, GPT-6 Astra, and Claude Opus. These projects host malicious installers alongside legitimate, signed executables from OpenAI and Anthropic, employing DLL sideloading techniques to bypass security protections. The campaign demonstrates strong operational security by avoiding dedicated command-and-control infrastructure, instead relying on Telegram, Tor, Catbox, and DNS over HTTPS. The malware chain includes YobaDropper and YobaLoader components that ultimately deliver unwanted software, including XMRig cryptocurrency miners, to infected systems. The threat actor exhibits indicators suggesting Russian origins and operates primarily in the UTC-4 timezone, excluding CIS countries from infection.

items.title: PHP2Shell (CVE-2026-109618/9) Havoc: UNC actors leveraging Public Exploit Code Against Public, Business And Educational Infrastructure
items.description: Two critical use-after-free vulnerabilities in the PHP engine, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, rated CVSS 9.2, affect the session.upload_progress feature. These flaws trigger during multipart request parsing before application code executes, bypassing WAFs and enabling unauthenticated remote code execution. Within 48 hours of the October 21, 2026 patch release, exploit code spread rapidly across GitHub. Diverse UNC actors deployed automated scanning and exploitation tools targeting over 70% of internet-facing PHP infrastructure running unpatched versions (prior to 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, 8.2.35). Observed campaigns include mass exploitation scripts, Mirai botnet C2 infrastructure, session poisoning chains via WordPress LFI vulnerabilities, and automated reconnaissance using proxy pools. Honeynet telemetry captured active exploitation from multiple IP addresses, demonstrating weaponization across public, educational, and business sectors globally.

items.title: DarkCore: A Data-Theft RAT With a Session-Hijacking Browser
items.description: Security researchers uncovered DarkCore, a remote access trojan distributed through cybercrime networks with advanced credential theft and session hijacking capabilities. The threat features a dedicated browser that reuses stolen session cookies to access Gmail, WhatsApp, MediaFire and other services while routing traffic through victims' IP addresses to masquerade as legitimate activity. DarkCore also includes hidden virtual network computing (HVNC) for concealed desktop access, credential managers displaying usernames and passwords, and reverse proxy functionality. Distribution occurs via PDF-themed shortcuts that download decoy documents alongside malicious executables. The native C++ tool communicates with command-and-control infrastructure via direct TCP connections and can load additional modules either in-memory or as temporary DLL files for extended functionality.

items.title: How VBScript Malware Evades Detection Using Trusted Tools Copy
items.description: Three malware campaigns using VBScript have been identified targeting victims primarily in Brazil and Portugal through phishing attacks. The campaigns deliver Overlord RAT, Lampion trojan, and an unknown RAT using fake legal notices, financial documents, and invoice pages. Attackers employ multi-stage execution chains involving obfuscated VBScript, batch files, and DLL side-loading with legitimate Windows components like VMware network libraries and VLC player. The malware establishes persistence through scheduled tasks and registry modifications while attempting to evade detection by adding Defender exclusions and checking for virtualized environments. Infrastructure analysis reveals Brazilian-based command and control servers, with payloads delivered through cloud services including Dropbox, Google Cloud Storage, and AWS S3. The campaigns demonstrate sophisticated techniques combining social engineering, trusted application abuse, and encrypted payloads to compromise systems and maintain remote access ca...

items.title: Lunex Unmasked: A New Information Stealer Deployed Through BYOVD
items.description: A sophisticated four-stage attack chain delivers the Lunex information stealer to Ukrainian-speaking users through fake CAPTCHA pages. The malware employs Bring Your Own Vulnerable Driver (BYOVD) techniques using AMD's PDFWKRNL.sys to disable kernel-level security monitoring before deploying the final payload. The stealer targets seven Chromium-based browsers, extracts credentials using custom SQLite parsers, exfiltrates cryptocurrency wallets, and establishes persistent access through PowerShell-based Chrome Native Messaging Hosts that survive binary deletion. The Lunex platform operates 28 command-and-control panels across 13 countries, features Russian-language operator interfaces, and demonstrates advanced engineering including PDB-guided kernel callback zeroing, custom encryption implementations, and direct syscall invocation. The financially-motivated threat actor originates from the CIS region and operates a Malware-as-a-Service platform serving multiple independent criminal operators.

items.title: Beyond testmetest: Native Addon Camouflage and 42 Armed GitHub Repositories Reveal a Hidden npm Publisher
items.description: Security researchers identified a sophisticated supply chain attack campaign involving 42 compromised GitHub repositories across 11 legitimate owners connected to the testmetest npm operation. The campaign evolved to use compiled native addons that decrypt hidden payloads at runtime, evading detection in CI environments through extensive anti-analysis checks. Attackers deployed polymorphic wrappers ranging from 12.9 to 13.7 MB that decode to identical publisher payloads, embedding execution hooks for AI coding assistants and IDEs. The operation included credential theft, repository hijacking, forged commit timelines, and automated malicious package publishing through GitHub Actions using npm trusted publishing. The infrastructure also links to shellpanel exploitation activities targeting cPanel systems. The campaign demonstrates advanced evasion techniques including environment detection for CI systems, containers, sandboxes, debuggers, and security tools before executing malicious code on developer workst...

items.title: Beyond the Inbox: How Threat Actors Abuse Microsoft Teams External Chat for Initial Access
items.description: Adversaries are exploiting Microsoft Teams' default external chat functionality to conduct social engineering attacks and deliver malicious payloads. Analysis of over 400 incidents reveals threat actors consistently impersonate IT support personnel using throwaway Microsoft 365 tenants with IT-themed display names marked as "(Internal)" to bypass external-user warnings. Attacks frequently begin with email bombing followed by Teams contact offering assistance. Adversaries leverage legitimate remote monitoring tools like Quick Assist, AnyDesk, and ScreenConnect to gain hands-on-keyboard access, progressing from initial contact to payload execution in under 15 minutes. Infrastructure patterns show a shift from default onmicrosoft domains toward paid top-level domains, particularly .top domains comprising 50 percent of observed cases. The technique exploits legitimate collaboration features rather than software vulnerabilities, requiring organizations to implement allow-list policies and user training to disru...

items.title: Gheist: Attempted Scaled Abuse of Stolen GitHub Tokens Stumbles
items.description: Since September 15, 2026, an automated campaign named Gheist has been performing mass abuse of compromised GitHub tokens. The attack commits a workflow named sync-check to every accessible repository, designed to print repository secrets into workflow logs. These secrets are then exfiltrated through GitHub's API and the logs deleted seconds later. Over 13,500 planted branches from more than 850 compromised accounts have been recovered, affecting personal projects and enterprise private repositories. While GitHub's approval controls have blocked exploitation in public repositories, private repositories and GitHub Enterprise environments remain vulnerable. The campaign uses no command-and-control server, carries the user agent 'gheist', and has been actively evolving with multiple variants. Approximately two-thirds of implicated accounts have been removed from GitHub, likely due to response activities.

items.title: deepveindrilling.com: Magento CMS block loader hits 953 stores
items.description: A criminal group has compromised 953 online stores, predominantly Magento shops, since July 2025 by injecting malicious JavaScript loaders into CMS blocks. The latest domain, deepveindrilling.com, was registered in October 2026 and employs sophisticated bot detection using browser fingerprinting to evade security scanners. The loader stores malicious code in visitors' localStorage for persistent execution. The campaign utilizes five different domains over 15 months, previously leveraging Keitaro traffic distribution system. Attackers exploited known Magento vulnerabilities, particularly PolyShell and SessionReaper file upload flaws, to gain initial access. The final payload targets cryptocurrency users with fake Ledger wallet pages. Most compromised stores were previously infected victims that were reinfected through persistent database access and backdoors, demonstrating the attackers maintain long-term access even after initial cleanup attempts.

items.title: Suspected DPRK Campaign staging PHP2Shell Targeting against Global PHP infrastructure
items.description: A Korean-speaking threat actor, tracked as the June 2026 Minjun campaign and linked with moderate confidence to North Korea's Lazarus Group, is actively planning targeted exploitation of two critical PHP vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619) that enable unauthenticated remote code execution. The campaign prioritizes government agencies, financial institutions, manufacturing, logistics, aviation, and trading platforms across the US, Japan, Thailand, Indonesia, Korea, Australia, Taiwan, India, Singapore, UAE, Saudi Arabia, and the EU. Operators are using AI-assisted reconnaissance to rank public exploit code and plan sector-specific attacks. Exploitation attempts have been observed globally since 17 October 2026, with 17 suspected source IPs identified conducting web shell deployment and session poisoning. The vulnerabilities affect all internet-facing PHP installations below version 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, or 8.2.35, with Apache mod_php at highest risk.

items.title: Inside the LiteLLM 1.107.0 supply chain compromise: Credential theft through Python startup hooks
items.description: On October 21, 2026, LiteLLM version 1.107.0 was compromised and distributed through PyPI and official container images. The malicious package leveraged Python startup mechanisms to execute credential-stealing payloads automatically, without requiring applications to actively import LiteLLM. Attackers utilized stolen developer GitHub credentials to redirect the release workflow to a lookalike repository. The payload targeted authentication material across developer tools, AI applications, cloud environments, browsers, and infrastructure. Two execution paths were identified: a credential collector launched through path extensions and a Unix-oriented loader persisted through site-specific configuration. Collected credentials were encrypted using AES-256-CBC with RSA-wrapped keys and exfiltrated to attacker-controlled infrastructure. The compromise affected not only LiteLLM gateway deployments but also developer workstations, CI/CD agents, test systems, and containers where Python was executed in affected env...

items.title: Infostealer riding the AI Train
items.description: Aokigahara is a newly identified infostealer with traditional data theft capabilities targeting browsers, VPN clients, cryptocurrency wallets, FTP/SFTP clients, password managers, and email applications. Its distinguishing feature is dedicated targeting of AI applications and development tools, including Claude, ChatGPT Desktop, Codex, Cursor, Windsurf, GitHub Copilot, and Gemini CLI. The malware collects authentication files, session data, and configuration files from these AI services, alongside developer credentials such as Git files, SSH private keys, and AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud credentials. Stolen AI credentials could enable unauthorized access to paid services, account resale, or data extortion. The stealer employs anti-analysis techniques including language checks, virtual machine detection, and control-flow flattening, and uses AES-256 encryption with X25519 key exchange for command-and-control communications.

items.title: ShinyHunters Renewed Mass Exploitation Campaign Targeting Oracle PeopleSoft
items.description: UNC6240, also known as ShinyHunters, has resumed mass exploitation of CVE-2026-35273 targeting Oracle PeopleSoft systems globally across multiple sectors including education, technology, healthcare, agriculture, transportation, and government. The threat actor bypassed web application firewall rules by URL-encoding a single character in the request path, accessing the vulnerable Environment Management Hub endpoint on systems where operators believed WAF rules had mitigated exposure. Following initial exploitation, UNC6240 deployed multiple web shells including x.jsp and u.jsp, a trojanized backdoor called SIDEEYE delivered via Ple64.exe, Neo-reGeorg tunneling tools, and MeshAgent for persistent access. The actor conducted reconnaissance, credential theft, and prepared for data exfiltration with established patterns indicating potential extortion activities.

items.title: PureRAT and PureLogs Campaign Targeting Japanese Organizations
items.description: Between July and August 2026, a sophisticated campaign targeted organizations across East and Southeast Asia using Japanese and Korean-language phishing emails disguised as product damage complaints. Recipients were directed to fake document-sharing websites that delivered ZIP files containing malware. The archives contained executables with double extensions and DLLs implementing various loader techniques including customized Donut loaders, Python interpreters, AMSI/ETW bypasses, process hollowing, and BYOVD attacks using vulnerable Lenovo drivers. Despite varying loader implementations, the final payloads consistently delivered PureRAT or PureLogs malware families. The campaign demonstrated advanced evasion techniques by frequently changing loader structures while maintaining the same core payloads, effectively bypassing hash-based detection methods. Infrastructure analysis revealed common sending patterns through PHP Swift Mailer and shared Feedback-ID values across campaigns.

items.title: The Psychedelic Stealer: When a CAPTCHA Becomes an Installer
items.description: Arctic Wolf Labs is tracking an ongoing campaign that compromises legitimate Ukrainian business websites and uses injected iframes to display a Ukrainian-language fake Cloudflare verification page. When a visitor interacts with the page, the lure copies a Windows Installer command to the clipboard and instructs the visitor to paste it into the Windows Run dialog. The command retrieves an MSI package that ultimately delivers a previously unidentified infostealer containing the embedded tag “Psychedelic.”

items.title: The Not So Silent Miner: Threat Actor Compiles Cryptominer on the Endpoint
items.description: A threat actor exploited a Samsung MagicINFO vulnerability (CVE-2025-4632) to gain initial access to victim endpoints. After three attempts, they successfully deployed a rogue AnyDesk instance using various download methods including certutil and PowerShell. The actor created a new local administrator account named 'oldadministrator' and disabled Microsoft Defender protections. Uniquely, instead of dropping a pre-compiled cryptominer, the threat actor compiled one directly on the compromised endpoint using Silent XMR Miner Builder.exe, executing multiple .NET Framework utilities and C compilers including donut.exe, tcc.exe, and MinGW64 tools. The resulting Monero cryptominer connected to the C3Pool mining service and ran under explorer.exe with suspicious command-line arguments. This compilation approach generated significant EDR telemetry, making the activity ironically conspicuous despite using tools associated with silent deployment.

items.title: RemotePanel and BoundSiphon: A Dual-Payload Toolkit for Persistent Access and Browser Theft
items.description: Two previously undocumented .NET malware components were delivered through a ClickFix infection chain. RemotePanel establishes persistent remote access by masquerading as the Windows Time service, providing operators with PowerShell control, file and process management, screen access, modular HVNC, and fleet management capabilities. It uses a BNB Smart Chain contract to dynamically resolve its active Command and Control server, enabling infrastructure rotation without rebuilding the RAT. BoundSiphon runs primarily from memory, targeting browser credentials and sessions, cryptocurrency wallets, password manager data, and documents, including secrets protected by Chromium App-Bound Encryption. Strong code overlap exists between BoundSiphon and a stealer previously documented by Socket, linking the sample to an earlier stealer codebase. The modular design separates persistent access from data theft, allowing operators to replace infrastructure and individual components while maintaining operational capabilities.

items.title: CARBONATO: a botnet built around an AI agent
items.description: ThreatDown researchers discovered CARBONATO, a Docker botnet that exploits exposed Docker daemons on port 2375. The operation was uncovered through an unauthenticated Docker registry exposed since May 2026, revealing two parallel activities: distribution of trojanized cryptocurrency wallet applications and a botnet infrastructure. The botnet leverages Hermes Agent, an MIT-licensed open-source AI framework, modified with a custom prompt directing it to execute commands via Telegram, maintain persistence, and harvest credentials. The campaign infrastructure spans multiple hosting providers including Linode, Hetzner, and Contabo, with activity documented from October 2024 through August 2026.

items.title: Konni Hackers Target Ukraine With Malicious LNK Files and VelvetCake PowerShell Malware
items.description: North Korea-linked threat actors are conducting Operation Conflict Compass, targeting individuals and organizations focused on Ukraine using spear-phishing emails with malicious ZIP attachments. These contain LNK files disguised as PDFs with themes related to Russia-Ukraine peace plans, Ukrainian research, and geopolitical issues. When executed, the shortcuts retrieve malicious files from GitHub, deploying VBScript to establish persistence via scheduled tasks and delivering VelvetCake, a lightweight PowerShell-based task runner. VelvetCake contacts command-and-control infrastructure to download and execute additional scripts that perform reconnaissance, collect system information, enumerate security software, and capture screenshots. The campaign also utilized trojanized Zoom installers and leveraged infrastructure in South Korea and Ukraine, with activity observed since early August 2026 targeting diplomatic entities, think tanks, and NGOs.

items.title: VeloCloud Orchestrator SQL Injection Vulnerability
items.description: VeloCloud Orchestrator (VCO) on-premises versions contain a critical SQL injection vulnerability that allows authenticated users with minimal privileges to escalate to superuser operator access. Any user with Enterprise Read Only role can exploit this flaw to access privileged internal functionality, potentially compromising the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of the orchestrator and managed data. The vulnerability is actively exploited, with specific malicious IP addresses identified. Affected versions include VCO 5.2.x prior to 5.2.3.18, 6.1.x prior to 6.1.3.10, and 6.4.x prior to 6.4.2.12. Hosted and dedicated VCO instances were already patched. Immediate upgrade to fixed releases is recommended, along with restricting web interface access and monitoring for suspicious activity.

items.title: SEO Poisoning Campaign Delivers New Armorsteal Malware
items.description: In September 2026, an SEO poisoning campaign distributed Armorsteal malware through fake websites impersonating Chocolatey package manager and Microsoft Activation Scripts (MAS) tool. Victims searching for software installation commands were presented with malicious PowerShell scripts that deployed Python-based malware protected by Pyarmor. The malware consists of three main components: a remote access module that communicates with command-and-control servers and verifies RSA-2048 signatures on received tasks; a surveillance module that logs keystrokes, monitors clipboard activity, hijacks cryptocurrency wallet addresses, and captures screenshots; and an information stealer targeting browser data, Discord tokens, cryptocurrency wallets, seed phrases, passwords, and SSH keys. The campaign employed anti-analysis techniques including cloud provider detection and code obfuscation, with infrastructure changes observed throughout the monitoring period.

items.title: StealC Is Back, and This Time It's a RAT
items.description: Four months after Operation Endgame dismantled StealC in June, its seller returned in October with Stadia, a full-featured remote access trojan that incorporates StealC's code verbatim. Unlike its predecessor, Stadia offers comprehensive remote administration capabilities including hidden desktop control, live command shell, file explorer, process manager, and in-memory loader, with the original StealC stealer functioning as one of six modules. The operator targets former StealC customers by offering a free month on the top-tier subscription priced at $900 monthly. Analysis reveals the binary shares byte-for-byte code with StealC version 3.5, particularly the Chromium App-Bound Encryption helper. The agent communicates via plain HTTP to three hardcoded IP addresses, uses RC4 encryption with Base64 encoding, and establishes persistence through hidden scheduled tasks under C:\ProgramData\ with randomized directory names impersonating legitimate updaters. The transformation from simple infostealer to full RAT...

items.title: Beyond the Sandbox: Leveraging Android Intrusion Logs to Expose Advanced Threats
items.description: Advanced Android threats increasingly operate beyond the standard application sandbox, requiring multi-layered detection strategies that combine on-device behavioral analysis with OS-level telemetry. Android's Delegated Scope enables enterprises to grant security applications access to security and network logs on managed devices without full MDM authority. The new Intrusion Logging feature extends similar forensic visibility to BYOD users through Advanced Protection on supported devices running Android 16 or later. This privacy-preserving capability allows users to collect and share encrypted security, DNS, and connection logs for analysis. The technical analysis demonstrates how these logs expose the complete RatHat attack chain, including Wireless Debugging self-pairing, ADB shell command execution, daemon staging, and command-and-control communications, providing actionable indicators of compromise across process execution, privileged operations, and network activity.

items.title: 2026 Year End Phishing Lures
items.description: As organizations approach year-end and fiscal close periods, employees face increased administrative activity in finance, HR, and IT departments. This heightened legitimate communication creates ideal cover for phishing campaigns. Attackers exploit year-end business processes by impersonating compensation adjustments, Q4 financial documents, access reviews, invoice follow-ups, and benefits statements. Multiple campaigns have been observed targeting organizations across sectors including aviation, telecommunications, manufacturing, real estate, technology, and financial services, with concentration in the Middle East. Attackers leverage SharePoint, Docusign, and Microsoft 365 themes, employing credential harvesting pages disguised as document-sharing portals. Generic protected-message lures prove effective by requiring minimal customization while appearing legitimate during busy periods when employees expect increased document requests and administrative deadlines.

items.title: RemControl: AI Built the Overlays. Victims Lose their PINs
items.description: Group-IB researchers discovered RemControl, a previously undocumented Android banking trojan operating as Malware-as-a-Service since May 2026. The malware targets over 30 financial institutions across Western Europe, the Middle East, and Canada through fake TVTap IPTV download pages distributed via malvertising. RemControl abuses Android Accessibility Service to inject phishing overlays, stream device screens in real-time, log keystrokes, and provide full remote control. The investigation revealed that the criminal infrastructure was inadvertently built using AI assistance, with complete AI-generated responses found verbatim in production phishing pages. The C2 panel documentation describes credential theft as quiz completion, suggesting developers deceived AI assistants into building fraud infrastructure under false pretenses. The threat actor UNKK operates the campaigns, with possible links to the Medusa UNKN affiliate botnet based on overlapping infrastructure patterns and naming conventions.

items.title: Mind the (Patch) Gap, Part 2: Fake Websites Used to Deploy Chrome & Windows 0-Day Exploits
items.description: In early September 2026, Chinese threat actor UTA0565 exploited unpatched zero-day vulnerabilities in Google Chrome and Microsoft Windows through sophisticated phishing campaigns. The actor registered fake domains impersonating legitimate organizations including China Digital Times and the Center for American Progress, sending targeted phishing emails to Asian government entities. Victims were directed to spoofed websites hosting an exploit chain leveraging CVE-2026-85046, CVE-2026-87491, and CVE-2026-85880. The attacks delivered CLEANGULP, a previously undocumented malware family with backdoor capabilities including command execution, file operations, and beacon object file execution. The malware communicated with command-and-control infrastructure via encrypted HTTP traffic using custom encoding. Multiple Chinese APT groups demonstrated coordinated access to this exploit kit, suggesting widespread sharing within the Chinese cyber espionage community during the vulnerability window.

items.title: Disposable Domains, Durable Hosting
items.description: Over five months, four distinct malicious chains operated through the same bulletproof hosting provider, AS202412 registered to OMEGATECH LTD in Seychelles. All chains began with fake CAPTCHA pages (ClickFix technique) that instructed victims to paste commands into Windows Run dialogs. The campaigns used disposable domains with similar naming patterns, compromised legitimate websites, and varied infrastructure including cloud storage, blockchain-resolved C2 addresses, and trojanized installers. Despite different payloads and staging methods, every chain initiated contact through AS202412. The provider expanded from initial allocations to announcing twenty-four /24 prefixes during the observation period. Most browser contacts ended at the lure page without execution, but successful compromises deployed stealers and remote access tools with persistence mechanisms surviving system reboots.

items.title: Open Season on Kapibala: Attacker Steals Over 18,000 Government Records Through WordPress Exploitation
items.description: A suspected Chinese-speaking threat actor, operating from UTC+8 timezone and linked to Red Heron, conducted extensive exploitation campaigns from May through September 2026. The adversary maintained persistent use of a single IP address to target multiple technologies including WordPress, ZyXEL switches, and various enterprise platforms. In the most severe incident, the attacker exploited WordPress vulnerabilities CVE-2026-63030 and CVE-2026-60137 to breach a western government organization, stealing over 18,000 sensitive records containing credentials and personally identifiable information. Additionally, the actor exploited CVE-2026-7273 in ZyXEL GS1900 switches, compromising 996 devices across 48 countries and exfiltrating configurations and credentials. The attacker demonstrated sophisticated capabilities including custom tool development possibly leveraging large language models, privilege escalation attempts, and systematic data exfiltration using PowerShell-based collection and staging techniques.
