items.title: ARTEX in the Wild: Storm-0940 Expands Targeting of IT and Software Vendors
items.description: Throughout October 2026, an actor utilizing ARTEX, an autonomous AI penetration-testing agent, targeted multiple IT and software vendors with attacks focused on identity providers including Okta, Entra, and Cognito. The activity overlaps with Storm-0940, a Chinese-state aligned actor involved in supply-chain attacks. Observed methodologies included mapping applications through JavaScript bundles and source maps, probing authentication mechanisms, manipulating OAuth callbacks, password-spraying corporate environments, abusing account recovery endpoints, and testing tenant isolation. Sessions lasted 24-30 hours with automatic IP rotation when blocked. The agent demonstrated agentic behavior through automated step chaining, output-based adaptation, and relentless iteration. Attacks featured coordinated bursts with unique user agents, one-second intervals between attempts, and targeting of software engineers across hundreds of users.

items.title: MythicRatatoskr: An Yggdrasil-enabled backdoor deployed in a UAC-0099-Sandworm collaboration
items.description: On July 16th, 2025, UAC-0099 conducted a spearphishing attack against a Ukrainian grain logistics company, deploying the MATCHWOK backdoor. The following day, attackers introduced MythicRatatoskr, a previously undocumented Go-based backdoor utilizing the Yggdrasil mesh network for command and control communications. This decentralized network enables end-to-end encrypted IPv6 traffic between nodes, complicating detection efforts. Approximately two months later, on September 17th, 2025, Sandworm executed a destructive data-wiping attack using the SDelete utility deployed via Active Directory Group Policy. This incident represents documented cooperation between UAC-0099, acting as an initial access broker, and Sandworm, responsible for the destructive phase. The MythicRatatoskr backdoor supports standard backdoor functionality including command execution, file transfer, screenshot capture, and SOCKS5 proxying capabilities, marking the first documented case of state-aligned actors exploiting Yggdrasil infrast...

items.title: TRUST#GRAFT : JavaScript-Compromised Sites Target WordPress Admin Browsers to Deploy a Persistent PHP Backdoor
items.description: TRUST#GRAFT is a sophisticated attack chain that exploits authenticated WordPress administrator browser sessions to deploy persistent PHP backdoors. The attack begins with JavaScript loaders that present fake Cloudflare-style verification screens while performing browser fingerprinting, credential harvesting from browser storage, and environment profiling. The critical pivot occurs when the script detects an active WordPress administrator session, automatically extracting CSRF tokens and uploading a malicious plugin disguised as 'Web Media Optimizer.' The PHP backdoor establishes persistence by copying itself to the must-use plugins directory, injects remote JavaScript into public pages, provides token-gated administrator access, and conceals itself from standard plugin management interfaces. The chain demonstrates coordinated infrastructure across multiple domains and requires no authentication bypass, instead leveraging existing trusted browser sessions to convert legitimate administrator workflows into ...

items.title: M365 Token Spray and Replay Campaign Compromises Business Email Accounts
items.description: Between July and September 2026, a sophisticated campaign targeted Microsoft 365 accounts through adversary-in-the-middle attacks and token replay techniques. The operation captured sign-in sessions via AiTM relays and replayed stolen tokens from IP addresses controlled by German hosting provider 1337 Services GmbH. Over ten weeks, 79 organizations were compromised with 497 successful sign-ins against over 200,000 failed attempts. Attackers registered 48 rogue Entra devices, replaced victim MFA methods, and created hidden inbox rules to conceal malicious communications. The campaign evolved through four distinct phases, rotating through different IP addresses and employing both scripted token replay and browser session replay techniques. In one case, compromised accounts were used to send payroll-related emails to external contacts, demonstrating business email compromise objectives.

items.title: Hunting Leaked PHP2Shell RCE Across Open Directories (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619)
items.description: Two critical PHP remote code execution vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, both rated CVSS v4.0 9.2, leaked before their scheduled patch on October 21, 2026. The flaws involve out-of-memory corruption in PHP core through multipart/form-data parsing, exploitable via session.upload_progress without authentication. Scanning began approximately 20 minutes after the patch release, with activity traced to a Mirai-style IoT botnet. Analysis of attacker infrastructure revealed approximately ten workspaces staging php2shell tooling, targeting WooCommerce, WHMCS, and Magento platforms. Despite widespread exposure affecting over 683,000 IPs running vulnerable PHP versions, no successful in-the-wild exploitation was confirmed as of October 21, 2026. The technical difficulty of achieving reliable code execution on systems with address-space randomization limited successful compromises.
tags: target:United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

items.title: Inside SiriusQT: A Seriously Skilled RAT
items.description: SiriusQT is a Windows Remote Access Trojan advertised on dark web forums since April 2026, offering capabilities beyond remote administration including HVNC, credential theft, cryptocurrency wallet collection, clipboard monitoring, keylogging, process injection, and persistence mechanisms. Distributed via Malware-as-a-Service by a reseller named GhostKernel, at least 30 users purchased licenses ranging from monthly to lifetime access. The malware was observed targeting victims in the United Kingdom, Germany, France, Spain, Italy, and the Netherlands. SiriusQT employs custom encrypted command-and-control traffic, multiple process injection techniques, and features both native C++ and .NET loader variants. The threat actor Amonus is referenced as the alleged developer, though GhostKernel appears to be the primary distributor through underground forums and Telegram channels.
tags: target:United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

items.title: New BlackX UEFI bootkit exploiting Baton Drop
items.description: In early 2026, a sophisticated APT campaign targeting diplomatic agencies in Tajikistan, Uzbekistan, and Turkmenistan deployed BlackX, a UEFI bootkit similar to the notorious BlackLotus. The bootkit exploits the Baton Drop vulnerability (CVE-2022-21894) to bypass Secure Boot and install malicious drivers into the Windows kernel. Despite patches being available since 2023, victims remained vulnerable because the mitigation requires manual activation by administrators. The campaign deploys cyberespionage payloads including a RAT using cloud storage for command and control, and OxiDLLRunner, a Rust-based payload. The attack demonstrates APT actors borrowing techniques from cybercrime operations, as BlackX appears to be reverse-engineered from BlackLotus code. Attribution points to APT41 based on code similarities and tactics matching previous campaigns.

items.title: LiteLLM PyPI Package and Docker Images Compromised to Steal Cloud and AI Credentials
items.description: LiteLLM version 1.107.0 was compromised through a supply chain attack affecting both PyPI packages and Docker images. The malicious release contains Python startup files that automatically execute upon Python initialization, stealing cloud credentials, private keys, browser data, and AI development tool authentication. Socket's AI scanner detected the compromise seven minutes after publication. Container build provenance reveals the attack used a lookalike repository (Berri-AI/litellm instead of BerriAI/litellm) in the release workflow. The payload targets AWS, Azure, Google Cloud credentials, GitHub CLI, SSH keys, npm/PyPI configuration, and AI tool credentials including Claude, Gemini, and Cursor. Stolen data is encrypted and exfiltrated to a command-and-control server. A separate loader mechanism enables remote Python code execution. The package receives approximately 23 million weekly downloads, making the impact significant.

items.title: PHP2Shell Vulnerabilities: CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619
items.description: Two critical remote code execution vulnerabilities in PHP, collectively named PHP2Shell, were disclosed on October 21, 2026. CVE-2026-109618 involves out-of-memory handling corruption that can interrupt PHP while internal request data is partially initialized, leading to invalid data treatment. CVE-2026-109619 exploits stale global state where request-owned internal state survives after memory is freed. Both vulnerabilities can be exploited successfully on ARM64 systems and x86 systems without ASLR. Fixed versions include PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, and 8.2.35. Over 2.6 million internet-facing hosts running PHP were identified as vulnerable, with 42% on end-of-life branches receiving no official patches. Early exploitation attempts were observed from multiple sources, including scanning activity and webshell deployment attempts targeting the upload-progress vulnerability path.

items.title: INC and The Gentlemen Ransomware: Exposed AI Infrastructure
items.description: Threat researchers discovered an AI-driven intrusion ecosystem operated by affiliates of INC Ransomware and The Gentlemen Ransomware groups through seven exposed command-and-control servers. The operators integrated commercial AI models via OpenCode and OpenRouter, logging over 8,000 messages across 133 sessions with recorded spending exceeding $23,000. They exploited edge devices at scale including FortiClient EMS, SimpleHelp, and cPanel systems, compromising thousands of targets. The infrastructure contained 46 custom INC encryptor builds staged for October 1, 2026 deployment, evidence of live victim encryption, and a custom arsenal including the Phantom autonomous framework, Ghost C2, and various exploitation tools. The campaign targeted 62 named organizations, predominantly in the United States, with focus on industrial manufacturing and healthcare sectors. OPSEC failures in late September 2026 exposed source code, credentials, AI session logs, and complete victim knowledge bases.

items.title: Stray Cat, Open Doors: How k0t Wanders Through the Network Edge
items.description: Group-IB and NyxLab uncovered a large-scale campaign by threat actor k0t exploiting FortiGate, FortiWeb, and Palo Alto GlobalProtect edge devices to harvest credentials and establish persistent access. The operation involves exploiting CVE-2025-64446 in FortiWeb and CVE-2026-0257 in GlobalProtect, alongside brute-forcing attacks using custom tools. Over 70,000 exposed credentials were discovered, with victims spanning multiple industries globally. Post-compromise activities include credential theft, Active Directory enumeration, and data exfiltration via Rclone to cloud storage. Persistence is maintained through MeshCentral, AdaptixC2, and various RMM tools including Atera and AnyDesk. The campaign shows overlaps with Qilin and The Gentlemen ransomware groups, suggesting k0t may operate as an Initial Access Broker, though direct affiliation remains unconfirmed.

items.title: Amazon-Themed ClickFix Campaign Serves Up Finger-Licking Malware
items.description: Attackers leveraged a sponsored Google search result for 'amazon business' to redirect victims to a spoofed Amazon login page hosted on Google Sites. The page presented a fake CAPTCHA (ClickFix) that tricked users into executing a malicious command using Windows' finger utility, an obsolete network tool repurposed as a living-off-the-land binary. This initiated a complex infection chain downloading IronPython, executing obfuscated Python scripts, and deploying multiple payloads including Doina malware, Lumma Stealer via a Node.js package, and a pirated NetSupport Client RMM tool. The attack infrastructure predominantly used barbecue-themed domains for command and control. The campaign affected multiple organizations and demonstrates cross-platform capabilities, with alternate payloads prepared for macOS users. Attackers employed sophisticated obfuscation techniques including Base64 encoding with Cyrillic character substitution, XOR encryption, and RC4 decryption throughout the infection stages.

items.title: "Next Exploit Opportunities": How a Threat Actor Used AI to Help Plan and Execute Multiple Types of Cybercrime Activities
items.description: A financially motivated threat actor operating under the handle BUGSTER leveraged jailbroken AI assistants, specifically the Hermes Agent framework with DeepSeek V4, to conduct multiple cybercrime operations across India. The actor, demonstrating limited technical skills but relying heavily on AI-generated scripts and reconnaissance, successfully exfiltrated over 5,200 personal records from a university database, conducted WordPress brute force attacks, and planned VoIP telecommunications fraud. Additional activities included Wi-Fi password cracking requiring physical proximity to targets, cryptocurrency whale reconnaissance, and development of credential scanning toolkits. The actor configured specialized AI bot profiles providing step-by-step criminal guidance, including fraud traffic ratios and carrier evasion techniques, demonstrating how AI lowers the skill barrier for cybercrime operations.

items.title: The Science of Exploitability: Decoding BlueHammer
items.description: BlueHammer (CVE-2026-33825) is an eight-stage local privilege-escalation chain targeting Windows Defender Antimalware Platform before version 4.18.26030.3011. It requires initial code execution as a standard user and chains CloudFilter callbacks, batch oplocks, object-manager symlinks, Defender's update RPC, offline SAM parsing, and SAMR operations to achieve NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM access. The exploit leverages legitimate Windows mechanisms rather than memory corruption, freezing MsMpEng.exe through CloudFilter manipulation while staging malicious update files. In laboratory testing, it successfully escalated privileges, recovered domain-admin credentials from LSASS, and enabled lateral movement via pass-the-hash to compromise domain controllers. Runtime factors including pending signature updates, WinDefend state, filter drivers, VSS, and CloudFilter reachability determine actual exploitability beyond version-based detection.

items.title: Recent AI-Assisted Cyber Attacks in Japan: Investigating Attack Infrastructure and Techniques
items.description: In October 2026, multiple organizations in Japan experienced unauthorized access incidents resulting in personal information leakage. Investigations revealed that attackers leveraged artificial intelligence to scan for known vulnerabilities and execute attacks through APIs. The threat actors analyzed Android application packages to identify and exploit APIs, testing for vulnerabilities including server-side request forgery. Multiple attack servers were identified containing tools for reverse engineering Flutter applications, analyzing Android apps, and targeting web applications, MySQL databases, Jenkins servers, and email gateways. Evidence suggests attempts to evade endpoint detection and response systems and deploy web shells for internal network access. The attacks also targeted web services beyond Japan, demonstrating a broader scope of malicious activity.

items.title: Autonomous LLMjacking: 'Skynet' Agent Hijacks Exposed AI Models to Run Attacks
items.description: Attackers have developed an autonomous offensive agent that scans the internet for exposed large language model endpoints and hijacks them to execute attacks. The agent is equipped with 74 offensive tools covering reconnaissance, exploitation of web frameworks including VS Code, Django, Jupyter, Laravel, Supabase, Next.js, Flask/Werkzeug, database theft through Prisma, credential harvesting, and cryptocurrency mining. Once connected to an unprotected model, it operates unattended for up to 100,000 steps without human approval. The operators use jailbreak techniques to bypass safety controls, redefining credential theft as routine development work. Victims include model owners who pay for computing power and compromised servers stripped of data and used for Monero mining. The activity was captured through an AI honeypot that recorded the complete instruction set, revealing a self-directed cybercrime operation targeting internet-facing AI services without authentication.

items.title: The Tale of Two INC Ransom Notes: A Ransomware Timeline
items.description: In late August, an organization was compromised by INC ransomware across at least 175 endpoints. The attack timeline spanned from early to late August with a 17-day gap, suggesting involvement of an initial access broker and a separate ransomware affiliate. Early August activity included scheduled tasks with randomized names and lateral movement via RDP using a compromised account. After the lull, attackers deployed AnyDesk for remote access, used Bring Your Own Vulnerable Driver tactics to disable security controls, and executed ransomware via Impacket tools. Uniquely, two ransom notes were discovered: the standard INC-README.txt and a subsequent DATALEAK_PRESS_RELEASE.txt containing detailed stolen file listings, threatening to contact media, employees, and partners within 48 hours to increase pressure on victims.

items.title: Inside a Global AI-Assisted Hacking Campaign
items.description: In October 2026, a Chinese-speaking threat actor conducted widespread AI-assisted cyberattacks combining the ARTEX penetration testing framework with multiple AI coding assistants including Claude Code, Codex, and Grok. The attacks, initially reported as targeting South Korean financial institutions, affected organizations globally across multiple industries including finance, retail, education, cryptocurrency, and telecommunications. Custom synchronization scripts maintained investigation context across AI sessions, while specialized agents divided reconnaissance and exploitation tasks. Prompts revealed requests for bulk personal data, transaction records, and mobile phone numbers, alongside questions about selling stolen information on underground markets. The workflow incorporated peer review between AI models, with GLM instructed to audit DeepSeek findings. Targeting spanned over 20 countries across Asia, Africa, Europe, and North America, indicating financially-motivated opportunistic attacks.

items.title: LiteLLM supply chain compromise
items.description: On October 21, 2026, attackers compromised litellm version 1.107.0, a popular Python proxy library for LLM providers with approximately 23 million weekly downloads. The malicious release was available on PyPI and official Docker images for about two hours. Attackers used stolen GitHub CLI OAuth tokens from three engineers to launch a private release workflow against a malicious fork. The payload installed a credential stealer targeting cloud, developer, AI-tool, browser and LiteLLM proxy credentials, plus a second-stage remote access trojan backdoor. The malware executes automatically whenever Python starts through dropped files in the site-packages directory. This represents the second supply chain compromise of LiteLLM in 2026, with no established connection to the previous incident linked to TeamPCP activity.

items.title: North Korea's Hangro Revisited
items.description: A deep technical analysis reveals updates to Hangro, North Korea's state VPN and mail product, operating on servers in Pyongyang and the Russian Far East. A new certificate hierarchy deployed in July 2026 differs significantly from the 2024 version, with both containing cryptographic anomalies where signatures fail verification. Investigation uncovered six network assignments in Chinese address space linked to a single registry contact associated with Silibank, plus infrastructure in Russian Far East networks designated KPOST. The service evolved from a commercial email gateway in 2001 to a certificate-bound VPN deployment issued to trade representatives through consulates. Technical evidence indicates structured infrastructure spanning North Korean, Russian, and Chinese address space, with mail systems configured for bulk transfers over intermittent connections using ten gigabyte message limits and ETRN capabilities.

items.title: PAYLOAD ransomware attacks through Active Directory GPO
items.description: In April 2026, a manufacturing organization in the Middle East suffered a ransomware attack where threat actors with domain admin privileges weaponized Active Directory Group Policy Objects to achieve domain-wide impact without deploying ransomware binaries on Windows endpoints. The attackers created malicious GPOs linked at the domain root, delivering ransom notes, hijacking wallpapers and lock screens, enforcing logon banners, and disabling local administrator accounts across all domain-joined workstations. No file encryption occurred on Windows systems; instead, the operation focused on encryptionless extortion through operational disruption and data exfiltration. Initial access was gained via compromised VPN credentials. The attack remained dormant for one day between GPO creation and detonation, evading file-based detection entirely by abusing trusted AD infrastructure.

items.title: Don't Call Us, We'll Call Your APIs | TraderTraitor Backdoors Resurface on Victim With No Crypto Ties
items.description: In 2026, the DPRK-sponsored Lazarus subgroup TraderTraitor continued campaigns targeting cryptocurrency entities, including a high-profile attack on LayerZero resulting in $292 million theft from KelpDAO. Following this disclosure, an additional victim was identified: a smaller IT services provider in India with no cryptocurrency connections. The compromise involved a DevOps engineer targeted through fake job interview lures containing weaponized Terraform coding projects. Malicious GitHub repositories used typosquatted provider domains to deliver macOS backdoors FLATROOF and ROOFDECK when victims executed terraform init. The backdoors enabled reconnaissance, credential theft, and cloud environment escalation. One day after LayerZero's public disclosure, attackers deployed an updated stripped version of ROOFDECK and removed earlier implants. Activity continued until June 2026, suggesting the threat actor ultimately abandoned the intrusion after determining insufficient value from the smaller target.

items.title: Threat Brief: Active Exploitation of PAN-OS CVE-2026-0257
items.description: Active exploitation of PAN-OS vulnerability CVE-2026-0257 has been observed, targeting GlobalProtect portal and gateway components. The authentication bypass flaw allows unauthorized attackers to circumvent security controls and establish VPN connections. Ransomware operators including Spikey Scorpius (Qilin) and Tarnished Scorpius (Inc), along with Settra ransomware actors, are exploiting this vulnerability to gain initial network access. Following successful exploitation, threat actors bypass multi-factor authentication, conduct internal reconnaissance using remote monitoring tools, move laterally via RDP and SMB, and stage additional tooling for credential harvesting and ransomware deployment. A sophisticated tactic observed involves pivoting directly to the virtualization layer, accessing vCenter management appliances, disabling security controls on ESXi hypervisors, and performing offline credential dumping against domain controller virtual disks. Multiple industries have been impacted including educa...

items.title: Ukraine's State Data-Exchange System Targeted by Russian-Speaking Operator via Graylog Log4Shell
items.description: Between May and September 2026, a Russian-speaking operator systematically targeted Ukraine's state data-exchange infrastructure by exploiting Log4Shell vulnerabilities in Graylog servers. The attacker swept 9.1 million Ukrainian IP addresses, filtering 7,576 live hosts to identify systems running UXP Verifier, a component of the national data-exchange platform. Using a two-stage CommonsBeanutils2 deserialization chain delivered through Graylog's sessions API, the operator gained access to at least two organizations, including a logging server containing 6.8 million documents from Ukraine's state data-exchange system. The operation was exposed when the attacker accidentally served their working directory over HTTP for 17 hours, revealing reconnaissance tools, shell history, exploit code, and access logs. While the operator queried transaction indices and demonstrated prior knowledge of the system's schema, no data exfiltration was directly observed. The campaign also included failed exploitation attempts a...

items.title: Midnight Mimosa Malware Campaign Exploits Android Firmware Supply Chain
items.description: Midnight Mimosa is a widespread Android malware campaign involving malicious applications preinstalled in firmware of low-cost MediaTek-based devices, with infections observed across more than 150 countries. The campaign leverages platform-signed system applications to silently deploy payloads, evade mobile security protections, execute remotely supplied code, and monetize compromised devices through advertising fraud and residential-proxy services. The malicious firmware components provide persistent system-level access before device activation, bypass conventional Android security controls by temporarily disabling Google Play Store protections, and maintain privileged positions while operators rotate payloads remotely. Affected devices include low-cost Android handsets, counterfeit flagship models, and devices associated with Doogee and Cubot products, with highest concentrations reported in Mexico, France, and Italy.

items.title: Inside Wazza: A Newly Observed Device Code Phishing Kit Targeting Microsoft 365 Accounts
items.description: A newly observed multi-stage phishing kit named Wazza has been actively targeting Microsoft 365 accounts since early July 2026. The campaign delivers phishing emails from compromised accounts containing PDF lures with business themes like invoices and contracts. These PDFs redirect victims through a complex infrastructure leveraging Google Sites, CloudFlare Workers, and various domains. Wazza features dynamic capabilities including 19 different phishing themes impersonating services like Adobe, DocuSign, and OneDrive, along with six corporate decoy websites. The kit employs sophisticated browser interrogation, anti-automation checks, and client-side protection mechanisms. The final stage abuses Microsoft OAuth device authorization, displaying a verification code and instructing victims to complete authentication on a separate page. Throughout the process, a backend session continuously monitors the authentication attempt, ultimately granting attackers access to victim accounts and cloud resources.

items.title: From Phishing to LLMjacking: Threat Actors Targeting Cloud Billing Accounts for LLM Usage
items.description: Threat actors are conducting sophisticated campaigns targeting Google Cloud Platform environments through phishing attacks via sponsored search ads. Attackers compromise privileged user credentials using fake login pages, then manipulate organizational policies to disable security guardrails. They create service accounts with Gemini API access, invite external attacker-controlled accounts, and assign administrative billing roles. The attackers link their external GCP projects to victim billing accounts, enabling them to execute large-scale AI workloads while hiding activity from victim monitoring. This results in unauthorized charges reaching tens to hundreds of thousands of dollars within 24-48 hours. The campaigns employ evasion techniques including geographic IP blending and demoting legitimate administrators to prevent detection and remediation.

items.title: Dissection of Operation FlashHole, a complex attack by Lazarus
items.description: In January, Lazarus Group launched Operation FlashHole against South Korea, exploiting mandatory security software CrossWeb EX through watering hole strategies and targeted spear-phishing emails with fake portfolio and resume sites. The campaign began in July the previous year, targeting software, construction, and cable equipment manufacturing sectors. The attack chain combines old and new malware families including TechHub, Cubridge, TouchShift, TouchHub, ClientHub, and LPEClient. Notable techniques include in-memory execution, GitHub and Dropbox for command-and-control infrastructure, DLL side-loading, and the incorporation of post-quantum cryptography (ML-KEM-1024) and GOST encryption. The sophisticated modular framework demonstrates Lazarus's continuous evolution of tools and tactics specifically designed for South Korean targets.

items.title: The Gentlemen: A closer look at a not-so-gentle ransomware-as-a-service operation
items.description: The Gentlemen is a Russian-speaking ransomware-as-a-service group that emerged in mid-2025 after operating as an affiliate of LockBit and Qilin. The group offers affiliates up to 90% of ransom revenue and has claimed over 800 victims across multiple regions and sectors. The ransomware targets Windows, Linux, NAS, and BSD systems using a double-extortion model that encrypts files and exfiltrates data. Written in Go, the ransomware employs ChaCha20 encryption with multiple speed modes, terminates security processes using vulnerable drivers, and spreads laterally through networks via PsExec. A May 2026 infrastructure breach exposed internal communications, affiliate information, and connections to the Qilin ecosystem. Organizations in the United States and Europe are most frequently targeted, particularly in manufacturing, technology, healthcare, professional services, and retail sectors.

items.title: Active Exploitation of CVE-2026-110936 in Siemens Software Center
items.description: A DLL side-loading vulnerability in Software Center version 3.5.8.7 is being actively exploited by attackers. The threat actors distribute a genuine, digitally signed copy of the application alongside malicious DLL files through unofficial channels. When executed, the vulnerable version loads the attacker-supplied DLLs without validation, enabling malicious code execution. The attack vector involves ClickFix social engineering tactics, tricking users into executing commands. The campaign uses specific infrastructure for payload hosting and command-and-control operations. Version 4.0.9.8 patches this vulnerability, with automatic updates applied upon application restart. No official systems or distribution channels were compromised during this campaign.

items.title: Swallowtail: Russian Espionage Group Targets Defense Firms in Two NATO Countries
items.description: Russian espionage group Swallowtail targeted organizations across two NATO member states, including a law enforcement agency, naval shipbuilder, and military aircraft engine manufacturer. During a two-month intrusion at the naval shipbuilder, attackers deployed the Hookedge backdoor delivered through malicious Word documents. They conducted hands-on-keyboard operations, stealing credentials through two distinct techniques: deploying an SSH private key to establish a persistent tunnel into the internal network, and using a PowerShell script to capture NTLM handshakes. The attackers also deployed a previously undocumented reflective loader (ld.exe) that decrypts payloads in memory using runtime-supplied keys. All targets hold information of direct interest to foreign intelligence, consistent with a broad collection effort against European government and defense sectors.

items.title: CVE-2026-102764: Critical BeyondTrust Remote Support Authentication Bypass Exploited in the Wild
items.description: A critical authentication bypass vulnerability in BeyondTrust Remote Support platform allows unauthenticated remote attackers to perform file operations without user interaction. Versions 26.2.3 and earlier are affected. BeyondTrust confirmed exploitation in the wild with two compromises dating to August 29, 2026, affecting one hosted instance and one self-hosted appliance. Mandiant investigation revealed arbitrary file uploads, deployment of SAWFLY web shell and BARECLAW tunneler, root escalation, credential-vault extraction attempts, persistence mechanisms, and log deletion. The activity is attributed to ARMORY CASTLE, a suspected PRC-nexus espionage actor. CISA added this vulnerability to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities list on October 16, 2026. Organizations must apply emergency patches and investigate for compromise, as patching does not remove persistence.

items.title: NetScaler intrusions chaining CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88779
items.description: In early October 2026, analysts investigated a compromise of a Citrix NetScaler ADC appliance running an affected 14.1 build. Attackers chained two vulnerabilities: CVE-2026-88771 (pre-authentication log-poisoning/RCE) and CVE-2026-88779 (SAML-parsing crash) to achieve root code execution. The intrusion deployed multiple persistence mechanisms including PHP web shells with cookie-based command channels, setuid shell modifications, cron entries, and boot hooks. Attackers installed TCP session managers, HTTP tunnels, and outbound reverse agents for command-and-control. A dedicated Go reconnaissance tool mapped internal infrastructure including DNS, LDAP/Active Directory, management services, and VMware vCenter systems. HA-aware persistence logic synchronized implants across appliance pairs and forced failovers. The campaign exfiltrated NetScaler configurations, historical data, and key material, demonstrating evolution from initial foothold to persistent platform for internal reconnaissance.

items.title: AOMEI Backupper update servers hijacked to push malware: Check your PC
items.description: Between April and July 2026, attackers compromised AOMEI Technology's update and notification infrastructure to distribute malware to users of AOMEI Backupper, backup software used by over 100 million people worldwide. During three confirmed tampering windows lasting ten, six, and five minutes, attackers modified download instructions to deliver a malicious ZIP archive containing an initial downloader that installed a persistent remote-access backdoor. The compromised infrastructure also serves AnyViewer customers. The brief tampering periods made detection difficult while limiting infection opportunities. The backdoor enables attackers to execute commands and install additional malware, leaving infected systems vulnerable to further compromise. Users can check for infection by scanning with security software, examining Task Scheduler for RadminComponentRuntime tasks, searching for unsigned upgrade-now.exe files, or monitoring suspicious network traffic to specific domains and IP addresses.

items.title: Plex vulnerabilities being exploited in the wild to drop a cryptominer
items.description: Multiple Plex Media Server vulnerabilities announced in September 2026 are being actively exploited to deploy cryptominers and proxy software. The exploitation chains together four CVEs to achieve remote code execution on vulnerable Plex servers. A honeypot deployment captured exploitation attempts from multiple IP addresses starting October 17, 2026. Attackers deployed XMRig cryptominer and myawesomeproxy software on compromised systems. The proxy tool potentially enables threat actors to utilize residential IPs for accessing corporate VPNs and email systems. Exploitation was observed from IP addresses 45.194.92.222, 91.92.40.202, and 176.65.139.228, with malicious payloads downloaded from 217.60.194.116. The vulnerabilities affect Plex Media Server version 1.43.2 and earlier, with proof-of-concept code publicly available through the plex2shell project.

items.title: QuartzLine: A working PDF viewer with a backdoor inside
items.description: QuartzLine, also tracked as CLOUDHAZE by Mandiant, is malicious software disguised as a functional Windows PDF viewer that conceals a backdoor enabling attackers to execute commands and deploy additional malware. The malware has appeared as paperline.exe and fielddesk.exe, signed with a legitimate but now-revoked EV code-signing certificate. Distribution occurs through malicious advertising, where users searching for unrelated content click ads and download the viewer from AWS S3 buckets. Once installed, QuartzLine establishes persistence through scheduled tasks and communicates with command-and-control infrastructure. Observed attack chains include Chrome data theft within one week of installation, followed by deployment of second-stage RATs like Caira and IronBark. The backdoor operates with user-level privileges and can execute arbitrary Windows commands.

items.title: ConnectWise (SkyKick) Vendor Credentials Abused in M365 Attacks
items.description: A Microsoft 365 API credential belonging to ConnectWise Cloud Backup (formerly SkyKick) was compromised and used to gain unauthorized access to customer M365 environments. The threat actor authenticated from IP address 144.172.64.128 on October 15, obtaining Microsoft Graph access tokens across hundreds of tenants. The attacker moved through tenants in sorted GUID order, suggesting automated targeting. In one instance, the ConnectWise Cloud Management MS Teams application elevated itself to Global Administrator and added credentials to other applications, including security tools. The activity began with password spraying against law firms on October 13-14, followed by role assignments in approximately 50 tenants, and culminated in widespread credential abuse. Nearly 1,000 Entra tenants showed sign-in activity from the malicious IP, with over 300 successful authentications. A second targeted wave focused on 16 tenants in policy, national security, trade, and critical mineral sectors.

items.title: CVE-2026-88771: Inside the Exploitation of a Critical NetScaler RCE Vulnerability
items.description: On September 27, 2026, Citrix disclosed CVE-2026-88771, a critical remote code execution vulnerability affecting NetScaler Application Delivery Controller and NetScaler Gateway with a CVSS score of 9.8. The vulnerability enables unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary commands without requiring optional features. CISA added it to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog following confirmed worldwide exploitation. Attackers employ a staged exploitation chain involving access-log poisoning, where malicious Base64-encoded payloads are staged in HTTP User-Agent headers, followed by authentication log poisoning using forged PPE failure messages containing shell commands. A vulnerable Perl diagnostic script then executes the poisoned commands with elevated privileges. Observed activities include web shell deployment, PHP enablement, and delivery of FreeBSD implants from infrastructure overlapping with CVE-2026-75650 exploitation targeting Adobe Commerce systems.

items.title: YuanKong RAT: the Android remote-control service that stamps its operators' names into every build
items.description: YuanKong is a multi-tenant Android remote access trojan whose dropper stores decryption keys in cleartext configuration files. The malware uses a two-key XOR scheme to unpack payloads signed with a shared certificate across all operator builds. Each build embeds operator account identifiers as hardcoded string constants, including account IDs, operator handles, and enrollment codes that are transmitted to command-and-control servers. Analysis of 110 dropper samples revealed 57 distinct payloads belonging to 42 different operator accounts. The RAT steals credentials through screen capture, accessibility service abuse, and overlay attacks while escalating privileges by self-pairing with the device's own ADB daemon to obtain shell access. It communicates via Socket.IO over WebSocket with a shared set of C2 domains.

items.title: An Analysis of Suo5-Based Tunneling and Pivoting Attack Techniques Through Case Studies
items.description: This analysis examines exploitation of Suo5, an HTTP/HTTPS-based tunneling tool, for pivoting attacks through compromised web servers to access internal networks. Suo5 relays TCP traffic and enables SOCKS5 proxy access to internal systems, supporting multiple transmission modes and environments including Java, PHP, IIS/.NET, and Nginx. Two deployment methods were observed: file upload exploitation on IIS servers through renamed ASPX files, and memory injection via Jenkins Script Console using Groovy scripts to register Suo5 as Servlet and Filter components. Key indicators include repeated POST requests in web logs, DLL files in Temporary ASP.NET Files directories, and PluginServletFilter chains in Java logs. Detection strategies recommend monitoring web request patterns, server-side behaviors, abnormal User-Agent headers, unauthorized URI access, and file modifications in web application paths, alongside restricting script execution capabilities and implementing network segmentation controls.

items.title: Inside Help TDS: Hotejka, Cloudflare Pages and Predictive Detection
items.description: Since April 2017, a Russian-language affiliate program called Hotejka, believed to be a rebrand of ROI777, has operated the Help Traffic Distribution System (TDS), delivering tech support scams to victims. The operation uses browser fingerprinting and geolocation to redirect users through compromised websites, malvertising, social media, and spam to fake Microsoft security alerts that lock browsers and display fraudulent phone numbers. When victims call, operators from call centers guide them to install remote desktop tools like UltraViewer, granting complete system access for ongoing exploitation. Since April 2026, Hotejka has created over 20,000 disposable domains on free Cloudflare Pages infrastructure, generating approximately 300 new domains daily. Affiliates including Balada Injector, Detour Dog, and DollyWay drive traffic to the TDS. Infoblox developed predictive detection algorithms that identify malicious domains approximately seven days before deployment, reducing customer exposure from 4% to 0.5...

items.title: BREAK THE SILENCE: Tracking Silent Lynx Through Exposed Infrastructure
items.description: Silent Lynx, a persistent cyber espionage threat actor, has conducted targeted intrusion campaigns against government ministries, diplomatic missions, and civil society organizations across Central Asia since 2024. The group focuses on high-value public sector organizations in Commonwealth of Independent States countries, leveraging spear-phishing campaigns through compromised government email accounts and malware staging via GitHub. Operations from late 2024 through 2026 reveal extensive infrastructure including exposed open directories, newly registered domains, and GitHub repositories. The actor employs lightweight reverse shells, PowerShell scripts, proprietary tools, and commodity utilities. Recent activity shows adoption of exploit-assisted delivery via CVE-2025-8088, expanding focus on Linux systems, and interest in FortiWeb vulnerability CVE-2025-25257. Attribution indicators point to Russian-speaking operators likely based in Kazakhstan, with targeting concentrated on water resources, environmenta...

items.title: ChainScript: Tracing a Node.js RAT Through the Blockchain
items.description: Blackpoint's Adversary Pursuit Group identified ChainScript, a previously unnamed Node.js remote access trojan discovered during ClickFix investigation. The malware disguises itself as legitimate software including Spotify, Zoom Workplace, and Microsoft Teams through malicious Windows Installer packages. ChainScript employs an EtherHiding-style C2 discovery technique utilizing a Polygon smart contract to dynamically locate active WebSocket infrastructure, enabling operators to rotate backend services without rebuilding agents. The RAT provides comprehensive remote access capabilities including interactive shell sessions, file operations, screenshots, payload deployment, cryptocurrency wallet discovery, remote JavaScript execution, self-update mechanisms, and cleanup functions. Multiple builds appeared under different names (ComponentTask33, UpdateDigital, HostShared, OrchidViolet66) while maintaining consistent core agent architecture. Analysis revealed automated contract deployment integrated into the mal...

items.title: Lazarus luring employees with trojanized coding challenges: The case of a Spanish aerospace company
items.description: ESET researchers uncovered a Lazarus attack against a Spanish aerospace company where attackers masqueraded as Meta recruiters on LinkedIn, sending trojanized coding challenges to employees. The campaign deployed multiple tools including LightlessCan, a previously undocumented backdoor that mimics native Windows commands to evade detection. Initial access was achieved through spearphishing via LinkedIn Messaging, delivering malicious executables disguised as C++ programming tests. The attack chain involved DLL side-loading techniques delivering payloads including NickelLoader downloader, miniBlindingCan variant, and the sophisticated LightlessCan RAT supporting 68 commands. LightlessCan represents a significant advancement over its predecessor BlindingCan, implementing execution guardrails and enhanced stealth capabilities. The campaign targeted aerospace technology and know-how for cyberespionage purposes, consistent with North Korean strategic objectives in missile development.

items.title: WeaselBiscuit Strips BeaverTail and OtterCookie Down to Essentials
items.description: A new JavaScript infostealer dubbed WeaselBiscuit has been discovered hidden in 11 malicious npm packages. This lean malware shares operational similarities with DPRK-linked BeaverTail and OtterCookie families but features a stripped-down architecture. WeaselBiscuit deploys through npm imports, executes a detached Node process, retrieves its payload from Npoint URLs, and communicates with a C2 server at 103.170.217.184:8787. The malware profiles infected hosts, steals Chrome extension storage containing wallet signing states, captures clipboard contents, and logs Windows keystrokes when commanded. Unlike its predecessors, it lacks wallet-draining code, browser password decryption, Python second stages, screenshots, and remote shell capabilities. The operation uses numeric campaign identifiers embedded in package names for tracking. While technical overlap suggests DPRK attribution, particularly through Npoint dead-drop patterns and nested IP geolocation lookups, definitive attribution requires additional c...

items.title: PolinRider Spreads Through Compromised GitHub Accounts and Packagist
items.description: PolinRider operators compromised a GitHub account to insert malicious code into development versions of visanduma/nova-two-factor, a Packagist package with over 700,000 downloads. The campaign spreads through compromised developer accounts and Git repositories across multiple ecosystems including npm, PyPI, Go modules, Packagist, and Chrome extensions. The operators use Git history rewriting, payload concealment in configuration files and font files, automatic execution through IDE tasks, and staged payload delivery via dead-drop mechanisms like EtherHiding and NullReceiver. Primary infection occurs through Git-based collaboration rather than direct package registry compromise, with PHP projects targeted using obfuscated JavaScript executed through shell_exec. The campaign appears linked to North Korean operators focused on cryptocurrency theft.

items.title: LabubaRAT Threat Snapshot
items.description: LabubaRAT is a custom, unsigned 64-bit Rust-based remote access trojan identified by Blackpoint, designed to masquerade as legitimate NVIDIA software. It provides comprehensive remote access capabilities including command execution, file operations, screen capture, and SOCKS5 proxying. The malware features configurable enrollment fields and an internal ZM_ configuration namespace, suggesting it is built on a reusable, multi-tenant framework consistent with a malware-as-a-service offering. LabubaRAT is managed through an associated backend infrastructure called LabubaPanel, hosted on German providers. The delivery mechanism utilized the RAT's own JavaScript execution capability. First observed in July 2026, it targets Windows platforms and employs various evasion techniques including masquerading as NVIDIA components and abusing legitimate Microsoft build utilities.

items.title: The Odyssey and trojans again: MovieReaper attacks users in multiple countries via compromised torrents
items.description: A previously unknown modular multi-stage framework named MovieReaper has been discovered targeting users through compromised torrent files. Attackers compromised the public torrent repository itorrents[.]org, enabling them to distribute malicious loaders disguised as popular movies, including "The Odyssey." The campaign began in mid-August 2026 and affected hundreds of victims across multiple countries. The malware employs a sophisticated infection chain with fileless execution, utilizing blockchain network Solana for C2 infrastructure resilience. The framework includes multiple stages: an initial loader with anti-sandbox checks, shellcode that retrieves C2 addresses from Solana blockchain, UAC bypass with persistence mechanisms, and a final file manager module providing comprehensive file system access. The campaign demonstrates advanced evasion techniques including manual API resolution, vectored exception handling, and in-memory execution.

items.title: Beware the SparroWock: The backdoor that bites, the commands that catch
items.description: ESET researchers have documented SparroWocky, a sophisticated C++ backdoor deployed by the FamousSparrow APT group since August 2025. This China-aligned threat actor has shifted focus to extensively targeting governmental organizations across Latin America, likely in response to increased US interest in the region. SparroWocky replaced the group's previous SparrowDoor backdoor and demonstrates advanced capabilities including reflective loading, anti-analysis techniques like SilentMoonwalk for call stack spoofing, and the ability to execute Beacon Object Files. The modular backdoor incorporates open-source projects directly into its codebase, uses TLS-encrypted communications with RC4 encryption for data exfiltration, and employs sophisticated evasion methods including MinHook API hooking and custom PE loading with host process camouflage. The targeting pattern reflects China's strategic interest in monitoring Latin American governmental responses to current US pressures regarding investments and infrastruc...

items.title: Ready, Settra, Go: New Settra Ransomware Variant Deploys MeshAgent RMM
items.description: Settra is a ransomware variant first observed in June 2026 that targets organizations through VPNs or compromised credentials. Two incidents were investigated in July and September 2026, affecting the consumer services, retail, and manufacturing sectors. Attackers deployed MeshAgent RMM for persistence, naming ransomware executables after victim domain names. The malicious activity included file encryption with .locked or .locked_wip extensions, deployment of RESTORE_FILES.txt ransom notes, clearing Windows event logs, and disabling Windows recovery options using reagentc and diskpart utilities. One incident featured Bring Your Own Vulnerable Driver (BYOVD) tactics using gdrv.sys. A notable operational security failure occurred when attackers misspelled the Windows Defender Event Log path, preventing its deletion. Both attacks followed remarkably similar operational patterns, with MeshAgent installations pointing to different C2 IP addresses (45.13.122[.]7 and 193.5.65[.]114), and malicious workstation WIN...

items.title: VectraRAT: An Undocumented Full-Stack MaaS Built From Scratch
items.description: VectraRAT is a previously undocumented Malware-as-a-Service platform combining a Go-based control server (VectraHub) with a native C++ Windows implant, renting from $250 monthly. The developer, operating under the handle 'Vectra' (formerly 'Nyxel'), has been active since August 2022 without prior public documentation. The platform offers hidden desktop control, keylogging, clipboard hijacking with cryptocurrency address replacement, browser credential theft, and a UAC bypass achieving elevation without user prompts. Delivered through Amadey loader and ClickFix campaigns targeting tax-themed lures, 48% of observed victims run corporate Windows editions including Windows Server 2025. Infrastructure analysis revealed exposed directories and operational panels across multiple hosting providers, with victims spanning the United States, Russia, Germany, and other nations.

items.title: SilkParasite Infrastructure: SpiceRAT Servers Tied to Energy and Government Targets Across Central Asia
items.description: Infrastructure analysis reveals a cluster of SpiceRAT command and control servers active from late 2025 through August 2026, linked through shared TLS certificates, domain registrations, and a cloned RTX Corporation webpage. The infrastructure connects to multiple threat families including SpiceRAT, NodeEdgeRAT, NomadRAT, and BloodAlchemy, suggesting either a single operator managing multiple toolsets or shared support infrastructure. A TLS certificate impersonating Uzbekistan's railway authority was issued by TLC, a Chinese state-affiliated certificate authority. Domains spoof Central Asian government entities including Türkmengaz, the Galkynysh gas field, Tojiktelecom, and Turkmenistan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Passive DNS analysis reveals subdomain infrastructure dating to mid-2022, indicating at least four years of ongoing operations. The infrastructure shares characteristics with previously documented China-nexus actors FamousSparrow and IndigoZebra, both known for targeting Central Asian governm...

items.title: Noodle RAT: A Recipe for Cross Platform Espionage
items.description: Noodle RAT, also known as ANGRYREBEL or Nood RAT, is a modular remote access trojan with dual versions for Windows and Linux, actively used by Chinese-speaking threat actors since at least mid-2016. Previously misclassified as variants of Gh0st RAT or Rekoobe, it is now recognized as a distinct backdoor family. The malware has been deployed in espionage and cybercrime campaigns targeting entities across the Asia-Pacific region, including Thailand, India, Japan, Malaysia, and Taiwan. Multiple threat groups including Iron Tiger, Calypso APT, Rocke, and Cloud Snooper have utilized this tool. Both variants feature shared command-and-control architecture, similar configuration structures, and modular capabilities. The Windows version operates as an in-memory backdoor with file management and proxy capabilities, while the Linux variant provides reverse shell, SOCKS tunneling, and task scheduling functionalities. Evidence suggests an actively maintained, possibly commercial malware toolkit.

items.title: How Money Laundering, Scams, and Espionage Hide in a Web Full of Casino Garbage
items.description: Illegal online gambling infrastructure spans three distinct cybercrime categories that defenders often overlook. First, over 1.7 million Chinese-language casino domains facilitate illegal gambling and transnational money laundering, primarily operated by triad-aligned syndicates. Second, thousands of "scambling" websites target global audiences with rigged games and withdrawal fraud, using deposit bonuses to lure victims. Third, China-aligned APT groups deploy the PeckBirdy malware framework within fake casino and adult websites as command-and-control infrastructure, targeting education, government, finance and technology sectors across Asia. These operations exploit U.S. and European hosting providers through infrastructure laundering while maintaining bulletproof Asian hosting. The campaigns have escalated sharply since 2023, with PeckBirdy domains achieving zero detection rates on VirusTotal. All three types appear visually identical, creating detection challenges for security teams.

items.title: The extension you never installed: KREMLIN forges Chrome's own integrity checks to steal banking sessions
items.description: Brazilian banking malware operation REF9334 has been deploying KREMLIN toolkit since May 2025, targeting Brazilian financial institutions through malicious browser extensions. The operation uses multi-stage JavaScript loaders, custom C++ installers, and exploits Chromium integrity mechanisms by manipulating Secure Preferences and regenerating required HMACs. Infrastructure leverages Ethereum smart contracts as dead-drop resolvers for dynamic C2 configuration. Seven distinct campaigns over 15 months show evolution from PULSAR RAT to REMCOS RAT delivery. Attackers impersonate twelve Brazilian banks through Portuguese-language lures, with transaction patterns clustering during São Paulo working hours. The malicious extensions intercept credentials, session tokens, and sensitive banking data through keylogging and request interception capabilities. Over 1,500 infections have been temporarily disrupted through network canary registration, with 98.75% of victims located in Brazil.

items.title: The banana stand: brokering and managing infections across Asia using MQTT
items.description: BambooToken is an emerging multiplatform malware family active since at least February 2023, utilizing the Message Queueing and Telemetry Transport (MQTT) protocol for covert command and control operations. The campaign targets Windows and Linux systems across Asia and South America, with infections observed on backend servers for mobile applications, legal and financial services, software companies, hotels, and GitLab instances. The malware leverages sideloading techniques through Tendyron's OnKey authentication software, commonly used in Chinese banking and government networks. Analysis reveals extensive host enumeration capabilities, plugins for antivirus detection, and potential keylogging and clipboard theft functions. Infrastructure analysis shows C2 domains ranking in Cloudflare's top 500,000, indicating widespread infections. The actor demonstrates sophisticated operational security, using MQTT's publish-subscribe architecture to hide infrastructure and employing Cloudflare proxies for additional o...

items.title: Fake MP4 File Carries Malicious Payload
items.description: A sophisticated infection chain leverages PowerShell loaders to deliver encrypted NetSupport client payloads concealed within fake MP4 files. The malicious MP4 containers appear valid to basic file-type checks but contain 6.5 MB of encrypted data in ISO Base Media File Format uuid extension boxes rather than playable video content. The attack begins with PowerShell delivered via Cloudflare-fronted infrastructure, performing environment checks before retrieving the carrier file. A secondary script parses the MP4 structure, extracts and decrypts an embedded 16.8 MB PowerShell payload, then deploys NetSupport Manager with silent operation configured. Infrastructure spans 40 live endpoints across six autonomous systems, primarily in Frankfurt and Los Angeles, with command-and-control gateways registered 77 seconds apart. The toolkit employs Russian-language business site decoys and rotates carriers frequently without backward compatibility.

items.title: skynox7: Proxyjacking Edge Devices Into Residential Proxies
items.description: A malicious cyber actor conducted a proxyjacking campaign, compromising at least 143 network edge devices across 34 countries to force them into residential proxy networks. The attacker exploited vulnerabilities in D-Link ShareCenter NAS devices, Ubiquiti UniFi Video NVR systems, and SAP NetWeaver Visual Composer, also targeting DVR/NVR devices from Hikvision and Dahua. The compromised devices were installed with Pawns.app software without owners' consent, monetizing victim bandwidth through IPRoyal's residential proxy network. The attacker configured SSH key authentication as a persistent access method. This activity was discovered when an organization identified suspicious authentication patterns showing multiple users logging in from the same residential proxy IP address, leading to confirmation of a serious intrusion.

items.title: Inside a PaperCut Attacker's AI Toolkit: Agent Instructions, Exploit Code, a Second RCE, and Victims Across 45+ Countries
items.description: Three exposed directories on infrastructure at 45.142.193[.]132 revealed an AI-orchestrated campaign targeting PaperCut NG/MF print management software. The exposed workbench contained AI-agent instructions, exploit code, operational logs, and post-exploitation tooling. Attackers exploited CVE-2026-81578 and CVE-2026-82078 through a Tapestry vulnerability chain, and developed a second RCE path via XML-RPC API abuse. The campaign deployed automated exploitation at scale using hundreds of AI agents running through OpenAI Codex and DeepSeek models. Post-exploitation activity included Windows credential harvesting, LSA secret extraction, reverse SOCKS5 pivoting using chisel, Metasploit automation, and Active Directory domain compromise. The actor's files documented 1,005 hosts across 45 countries in their reconnaissance pool, with 46 confirmed Active Directory domain compromises and 45 targets maintaining live internal access pivots at time of discovery.

items.title: KGB RAT: A Fully Undetectable Windows Trojan Built to Spy, Steal, and Terrorize
items.description: KGB RAT is a Windows Remote Access Trojan actively promoted on underground forums since late 2025, marketed deceptively as a legitimate administration tool. Sold through a Malware-as-a-Service model with pricing from $150 to $800, it features credential theft, keylogging, hidden desktop takeover, ransomware capabilities, and psychological harassment functions including screamers and forced blue screens. The tool ships with a built-in FUD crypter updated daily to evade Windows Defender, requires no port forwarding for C2 connectivity, and delivers Telegram-based notifications. Evidence suggests development began in early 2022. Based on NjRAT foundation, it targets multiple operators sharing a common builder, with at least one deployment featuring an active CryptoClipper module for cryptocurrency wallet address swapping.

items.title: AI-Powered Espionage Campaign Targets Government Linux Infrastructure
items.description: An espionage campaign tracked as CL-UNK-1211 targeted government entities and state-affiliated infrastructure between October 2025 and April 2026, utilizing AI-generated payloads containing conversational annotations suggesting LLM or automated AI agent involvement. Attackers focused on Linux environments deploying web shells, custom cross-platform backdoors including SysGoRAT malware, and open-source tools to maintain persistent access. Operations included extensive reconnaissance, database dumping, mailbox enumeration targeting social media accounts linked to government emails, and sophisticated defense evasion techniques such as disabling endpoint protections, erasing system logs, and planting deceptive red-team markers to disguise malicious activity as legitimate security assessments.

items.title: Variola: From ClickFix to a Modular Implant
items.description: Blackpoint's Adversary Pursuit Group traced a ClickFix intrusion to a previously unclassified modular Windows implant designated Variola. The malware establishes persistent host identity through encrypted storage, maintains configuration and controller information across executions, and employs authenticated command-and-control with controller rotation capabilities. Variola's modular architecture enables operators to dynamically load additional components for credential theft, browser manipulation, and session hijacking. The framework demonstrates capabilities typical of banking trojans, including Chromium browser process injection, live cookie database access, and VNC-style remote access. Multiple related builds discovered in the same GitHub repository suggest active development and experimentation. The implant uses XSalsa20 encryption, secp256k1 key exchange, and Ed25519 signatures for secure communications. Its ability to preserve context, migrate between processes, and expand capabilities on demand tra...

items.title: ARMORY CASTLE Exploits BeyondTrust
items.description: On October 15, BeyondTrust disclosed CVE-2026-102764, a vulnerability affecting BeyondTrust Remote Support appliances that enables arbitrary file upload. Mandiant identified ARMORY CASTLE, a suspected PRC-nexus espionage actor, exploiting this as a zero-day in late August 2026. Following exploitation, the actor deployed SAWFLY webshell and BARECLAW tunneler, escalated privileges using SUID bit manipulation, harvested credentials from the BeyondTrust vault, and established persistent access by modifying sudoers templates and HAProxy configurations. The actor demonstrated deep knowledge of BeyondTrust internals, abusing proprietary CLI utilities and reverse-proxy routing. They systematically deleted logs to evade detection and leveraged compromised administrator credentials to pivot laterally and exfiltrate sensitive documents. Organizations face potential widespread exploitation as ARMORY CASTLE historically conducts opportunistic campaigns following vulnerability disclosure. Immediate patching and comprehe...

items.title: Aoki: Infostealer Targets AI Coding Assistant Credentials
items.description: The Aoki infostealer has evolved to target credentials from AI coding assistants including Claude, OpenAI's Codex, Cursor, Codeium and Gemini. This capability represents a recent addition, as earlier versions did not target AI-related files. The malware steals API keys, tokens and session files that could enable attackers to conduct activities under legitimate user identities, access connected repositories, cloud services and CI/CD pipelines. Beyond AI credentials, Aoki harvests data from dozens of browsers, cryptocurrency wallets, password managers, messaging applications, gaming platforms, VPN and FTP clients. The malware collects available data and transmits it to command-and-control servers. This development suggests AI credentials are becoming as valuable as traditional targets like payment card data and cryptocurrency wallets for cybercriminals.

items.title: Exposing AdFection: How Discover-Tech Turned Targeted Ads Into a Pipeline for Zero-Click Mercenary Spyware
items.description: This investigation reveals the first public confirmation of zero-click mercenary spyware delivered via targeted advertisements, termed AdFection. Devices at Al Jazeera were infected with Candiru spyware through malicious ads purchased by Israeli company Discover-Tech, which operates as a facilitator for mercenary spyware partners. Discover-Tech's Controlium platform enables partners to de-anonymize, fingerprint, and automatically infect devices when advertisements render. Analysis of four billion bidding records shows ads were displayed across nearly 200,000 websites and apps in dozens of countries. The company appeared on Google and IAB Europe vendor lists from 2020-2026, serving ads via major networks. Discover-Tech is linked to multiple mercenary surveillance actors including Candiru, Intelos, and Bindecy, and supports mass-deanonymization through mobile carrier vulnerability exploitation. The infrastructure also covertly directed millions of devices to contact Candiru servers for tracking and reconnais...

items.title: DragonForce Ransomware Profile: From Affiliate Program to Cybercrime Cartel
items.description: DragonForce is a financially motivated ransomware operation that emerged in August 2023, initially using leaked LockBit 3.0 code and later transitioning to Conti v3-based variants. Operating as a Ransomware-as-a-Service model, they offer affiliates an 80% revenue share and comprehensive management tools. By March 2025, they evolved into a 'cartel' structure, providing white-label services. Their attacks primarily target organizations in the US and UK, spanning multiple sectors including manufacturing, professional services, retail, healthcare, and technology. The group actively recruits developers and reverse engineers while offering specialized data analysis services to help affiliates maximize extortion pressure. Notable incidents include a major MSP breach in May 2025 exploiting SimpleHelp vulnerabilities, cascading compromise across multiple client networks.
