items.title: Hirudo: From Fake Updates to Patched Banking Apps
items.description: A new Android banking remote access trojan named Hirudo has been identified, combining credential theft with live remote control. It is delivered through shopping and entertainment apps that act as droppers, installing the trojan as a separate package behind fake update prompts. The malware replaces legitimate banking applications with patched versions that disable security checks from within the app itself. Eight Indonesian banking apps covering seven banks have been targeted with purpose-built replacements embedding a hooking engine. The campaign uses real advertising infrastructure including Amazon CloudFront for distribution, with targeting extending beyond Indonesia to China, India, Mexico, Morocco, Thailand, and Malaysia. Backend data from August 2026 revealed thousands of stolen credentials and device records.

items.title: Ivanti CVE-2026-104935: Zero-Day Chain Exploited in Operation Innovate
items.description: Ivanti has released emergency security updates after attackers exploited a chain of three zero-day vulnerabilities in Connect Secure VPN appliances to gain root-level access without authentication. The attack began on October 3, targeting an appliance running version 22.8R2.4. Two vulnerabilities are tracked as CVE-2026-104935 with a CVSS score of 8.6, involving an authentication bypass and remote code execution through manipulated CGI requests and malicious file uploads. A third unpatched vulnerability allows privilege escalation to root by manipulating a privileged service through memory modification. While patches address the authentication bypass and RCE, the privilege escalation flaw remains unresolved. CISA added the vulnerability to its KEV catalog with an October 16 remediation deadline for federal agencies.

items.title: Fake Calendly "Meta Careers" pages steal Facebook and Google logins
items.description: A wave of fraudulent websites mimicking Calendly booking pages for Meta job interviews has been identified, targeting job seekers to steal credentials. Victims select interview time slots, provide personal information, and complete fake CAPTCHA verifications before being prompted to log into Facebook and Google accounts. The sophisticated phishing kit captures login credentials and bypasses two-factor authentication by relaying authentication codes in real-time to attackers. The pages use convincing replicas of legitimate login screens with fake address bars displaying authentic URLs. Eleven domains following similar naming patterns have been identified, utilizing generic recruiting-related terms. The collection infrastructure operates through Amazon API Gateway in Singapore, with code comments in Vietnamese suggesting the operation's possible origins.

items.title: Disruption Targets Major Chinese-Language Phishing Kits with Japanese Focus
items.description: A coordinated disruption action targeted Chinese-speaking cybercriminals operating three major phishing kits: CoGUI, CoAceV, and CoFish_Ws, which collectively distributed hundreds of millions of credential phishing messages primarily targeting Japanese organizations. These operations impersonated 66 well-known brands, mainly consumer and finance companies, to steal usernames, passwords, and payment data. The threat actors demonstrated sophisticated capabilities, utilizing approximately 17,000 unique domains with frequent rotation and evasion techniques. The ecosystem enablers YAM Store and Iron Man were also targeted through a civil lawsuit and domain seizures, conducted in collaboration between Microsoft, Health-ISAC, and multiple security partners. This coordinated action is expected to significantly impact the Chinese phishing ecosystem and cause substantial operational disruption to multiple threat groups conducting financial fraud.

items.title: PEERSTITCH, a Stealthy FortiGate Implant
items.description: A sophisticated multi-stage network intrusion against a telecommunications organization in September 2024 exploited CVE-2024-47575 on a FortiManager appliance, exfiltrating configurations and cryptographic material for over 500 managed FortiGate firewalls. Attackers then exploited CVE-2025-61624 to deploy PEERSTITCH, a novel memory-resident ARM64 malware that leaves no disk artifacts or network traces. The implant operates by patching running processes, creating covert inter-process communication channels between system daemons, and intercepting network traffic. Additional attack vectors included weaponizing Apache mod_md for reverse shell command and control, impersonating the FortiManager platform to compromise downstream devices, and deploying extensive anti-forensic measures. The intrusion demonstrates advanced tradecraft consistent with nation-state actors, highlighting the critical risk of centralized edge management platforms.

items.title: How AI Agents Turned One Exposed Endpoint into a Server Takeover
items.description: An investigation revealed the first confirmed incident where large language model-driven AI agents executed substantial portions of an attack. Within 24 hours, attackers exploited an exposed job-submission feature on an Apache Tomcat server running Spring Batch, requiring no authentication, zero-days, or new malware. The attacker used Cairn, an open-source AI agent orchestration platform, identified on the attacking infrastructure. Commands were executed through JavaScript via Nashorn engine, with results extracted through error messages in 1,800-byte chunks across hundreds of sequential requests. The attacker recovered plaintext database credentials from configuration files, enabled xp_cmdshell, and escalated privileges using PrintSpoofer and GodPotato tools to achieve SYSTEM access. Registry hives were extracted, administrator accounts created, and artifacts deleted. Machine-driven execution was evidenced by rapid command timing, programmatic job naming, structured output formatting, and automated error ...

items.title: Iron Man & YamStore: Powering a Global Phishing-as-a-Service Ecosystem
items.description: Resecurity identified and mapped infrastructure supporting a commercial Phishing-as-a-Service operation marketed as 'Iron Man System.' The kit is sold to criminal buyers as a self-hosted package deploying pre-built lure pages impersonating postal services, banks, government agencies, and other trusted entities. Through infiltration of Chinese threat actor communities and acquisition of a license, Resecurity traced the back-end infrastructure and found 2,360 phishing templates targeting 130 countries. The operation features a self-hosted build registry with 911 published versions, bilingual Chinese-English interface, and subscription-based licensing tied to vendor-controlled authorization servers. Working with Microsoft's Digital Crimes Unit and industry partners, the cybercriminal infrastructure was mapped and disrupted. The kit captured approximately 17.4GB of telemetry data targeting 75,000 organizations through an estimated 1 billion phishing emails.

items.title: Thai Broadband Provider Targeted via FortiGate SSL-VPN and MeshCentral Persistence
items.description: An exposed directory on a Thai server revealed an active intrusion campaign targeting 3BB (Triple T Broadband), one of Thailand's largest broadband providers. The attacker exploited CVE-2024-21762 in a FortiGate 60F SSL-VPN appliance to gain initial access, then deployed MeshCentral remote management software for persistent command-and-control. The operation involved extensive reconnaissance, credential harvesting targeting RADIUS authentication databases, privilege escalation using PwnKit and Dirty COW exploits, lateral movement via SSH brute-forcing across 55+ internal hosts, and anti-forensic cleanup procedures. Multiple devices were already enrolled under attacker control at discovery, with additional targeting of Jasmine International infrastructure. The attacker's toolkit included web application exploitation scripts, database credential extraction tools, and persistence mechanisms designed to maintain long-term access to subscriber authentication systems.

items.title: Case of AgentTesla Malware Distribution Disguised as a Business Proposal Email
items.description: A phishing campaign has been observed distributing AgentTesla infostealer through emails masquerading as business proposal requests. Recipients are asked to review an attached product list, but the ZIP file contains an executable file instead of a document. The malicious EXE disguises itself as a café management program using Chinese-language descriptions and UI elements. Through multiple stages of obfuscation, the malware extracts encrypted data from bitmap resources, performs XOR decryption, and loads successive .NET payloads into memory. The final payload is AgentTesla, which steals credentials, cookies, and contact information from browsers, email clients, FTP and VPN applications. Stolen data is exfiltrated via FTP to a compromised server. The attack demonstrates sophisticated multi-stage loading techniques and social engineering tactics targeting business users.

items.title: ClingSTUN Turns Vulnerable Edge Devices Into Attacker Infrastructure
items.description: An evolving Linux malware campaign deploys ClingSTUN, a back-connect proxy backdoor exploiting known vulnerabilities in Internet-facing IoT and network devices. The malware establishes persistent access and converts compromised systems into remotely controlled proxy nodes. Supporting multiple Linux architectures, ClingSTUN combines boot persistence, process termination, watchdog manipulation, process concealment, remote command execution, and self-propagation. It abuses legitimate public STUN infrastructure for NAT traversal. The campaign has expanded the number of vulnerabilities and device vendors it targets over time, affecting products from D-Link, EnGenius, Realtek, TP-Link, AVTECH, Ivanti, Tenda, Lantronix, and others, highlighting the continued risk posed by unpatched, unsupported, and unnecessarily exposed Internet-facing devices.

items.title: 2026 Q3 Linux SSH Server Targeted Malware Statistics Report
items.description: During Q3 2026, honeypot monitoring revealed attacks targeting poorly managed Linux SSH servers through brute force and dictionary attacks. Primary malware families included ShellBot (also known as PerlBot), a Perl-based DDoS bot with C&C infrastructure at specific IPs, and Fisieredoor, a backdoor capable of executing commands and deploying SSH dictionary attack tools. Attackers downloaded malware using wget or curl, then installed user-mode rootkits, XHide process masking tools, and XMRig cryptocurrency miners. The launcher malware utilized ld.so.preload to inject rootkits and disguised mining processes as legitimate bash sessions. Fisieredoor deployed additional tools including goauto and tsm for credential harvesting and lateral movement, transmitting successful authentication results to command servers.

items.title: Q3 2026 Statistical Report on Malware Targeting Windows Database Servers
items.description: During the third quarter of 2026, attackers targeted MS-SQL and MySQL servers on Windows systems through multiple attack vectors including brute-force attacks, dictionary attacks, and vulnerability exploitation. Threat actors deployed XMRig cryptocurrency miners, GotoHTTP backdoors, and SoftEther VPN infrastructure along with various web shells including Sharp4WebCmd, Suo5, and PowerShell-based shells for persistence. Additional tools used included VShell for remote command execution, HackBrowserData for credential theft, Fscan for network reconnaissance, and Cloudflared for port exposure. Attackers created backdoor accounts for RDP access and operated SoftEther VPN servers in Cascade Connection mode as command and control infrastructure. The attacks primarily resulted from weak passwords, improper account management, and inadequate security measures on externally exposed database servers.

items.title: 2026 Third Quarter Windows Web Server Targeted Malware Statistics Report
items.description: This analysis examines attacks against Windows web servers during Q3 2026, focusing on Internet Information Services (IIS) and Apache Tomcat environments. Attackers exploited unpatched vulnerabilities, misconfigurations, and weak management practices to gain control through webshell uploads, remote code execution, proxy tools, and privilege escalation utilities. Two prominent attack cases involving CVE-2019-18935 in Telerik UI for ASP.NET AJAX are detailed. The first case deployed reverse shells connecting to 206.82.6.22, utilized Potato-family privilege escalation tools like SweetPotato and PrintSpoofer to obtain SYSTEM privileges, and installed Godzilla-style memory webshells. The second case leveraged the same vulnerability to deploy a Rust-based scanner that identified WordPress installations and reported findings via Telegram. Attackers subsequently conducted coin mining, established VPN servers, and maintained persistent remote access. Recommendations include applying current patches, minimizing exte...

items.title: RSVP to Disaster: How One Click Installs a RAT
items.description: Cybercriminals are exploiting digital event invitations to distribute remote access trojans. Victims receive legitimate-looking emails with generic subject lines about special gatherings and celebrations. The messages contain download buttons that redirect users through fake CAPTCHA verification pages hosted on recently created domains. After verification, users encounter another generic invitation page prompting them to download an eInvite file. This delivers a zipped folder containing ScreenConnect.exe, a legitimate ConnectWise Screen Connect installer weaponized as a RAT. Once executed, attackers gain full remote access to compromised devices through an unassuming taskbar icon that reveals an active connection. The campaign leverages user curiosity rather than sophisticated techniques, making it particularly effective during holiday seasons when event invitations are common.

items.title: Clean Install, Stolen Creds: Fake WatchGuard VPN Site Serves Genuine Signed Client
items.description: In early October, a sophisticated credential phishing campaign targeted WatchGuard Mobile VPN users through a fake download site at watchguard-vpn[.]net. The attack used SEO poisoning to appear in search results and deployed a unique technique: after collecting victim credentials twice through browser pop-ups, it downloaded the genuine, validly signed WatchGuard installer directly from WatchGuard's official CDN. This eliminated malicious files that security tools could detect. The first credential submission was deliberately rejected as incorrect to collect multiple passwords. The credential collection endpoint at watchguard-ssl[.]online received server addresses, usernames, and passwords, providing attackers network access. This domain was previously reported in January with no backend functionality but was re-registered in August with full phishing capabilities implemented by September.

items.title: Statistical Report on Malware Targeting Linux SSH Servers in the Third Quarter of 2026
items.description: During the third quarter of 2026, multiple attack campaigns targeted poorly managed Linux SSH servers using brute force, dictionary attacks, and vulnerability exploits. Threat actors deployed ShellBot, a Perl-based DDoS bot, utilizing C&C servers at specific IP addresses with capabilities including port scanning and UDP flooding. A sophisticated attack chain involved launcher malware that executed user-mode rootkit libSSL2.3.0.So via /etc/ld.so.preload, subsequently deploying XMRig cryptocurrency miner disguised as -bash using XHide process concealment tool. Additionally, Fisieredoor backdoor was deployed, capable of command execution and installing SSH brute-force tools including goauto and tsm-family, which systematically targeted systems using credential lists. Organizations must implement strong password policies, regular patching schedules, and access controls for externally exposed SSH infrastructure.

items.title: Kimsuky attacks targeting Ukrainian experts in diplomacy, security, and international policy
items.description: The Kimsuky threat group has launched spear phishing campaigns targeting Ukrainian experts in diplomacy, security, and international policy through fraudulent international conference invitations and collaboration requests. This operation, dubbed GitPower, leverages legitimate development platforms like GitHub for malware distribution and data exfiltration. Attack vectors include malicious LNK files and fake Zoom installers, demonstrating links to previous CHM-based attack methodologies. The campaign appears to be state-sponsored cyber espionage focused on monitoring cooperation developments between South Korea and Ukraine. Organizations are advised to enhance EDR detection capabilities and implement threat hunting for suspicious LNK file execution, PowerShell abuse, and unauthorized GitHub communications.

items.title: The phone was compromised before the user turned it on: the rise of Midnight Mimosa
items.description: A sophisticated malware campaign targets low-cost Android devices built on MediaTek platforms, with malicious code preinstalled in device firmware before users receive them. The platform-signed system application operates with elevated privileges, enabling operators to silently install applications, grant permissions, and load remote code. The scheme primarily generates revenue through ad fraud, click fraud, device information collection, and converting infected devices into residential-proxy botnet nodes. The malicious system application ships under various system-sounding names including com.android.system.lite, com.android.sys.prot, and com.android.sys.gmsprot. Operators deploy at least 32 disguised applications including fake weather, app-lock, and OCR tools. The malware disables Google Play Store during payload installation to evade detection, then re-enables it afterward. Thirteen related applications were also discovered on Google Play, communicating with identical command-and-control infrastructure...

items.title: From WhatsApp to SYSTEM: Inside the VulcanRAT207.A Intrusion Chain
items.description: A sophisticated multi-stage intrusion chain begins with a WhatsApp-delivered financial document lure carrying Statement.exe. The malware employs NRV2E compression to conceal its true payload, which performs extensive host screening before attempting privilege elevation via COM-based techniques. Using PoolParty Variant 7 injection, the loader transfers execution into the Windows Task Scheduler process under LocalSystem authority. A downloader shellcode retrieves a compound bundle from a remote server, which deploys through a reflective loader. The deployment stage utilizes a signed GoFly driver to terminate Baidu security processes, establishes persistence via DLL side-loading with a legitimate Intel-signed VulkanInfo executable, and launches a WebSocket-based remote access trojan. The final VulcanRAT207.A payload provides extensive surveillance capabilities including shell access, keystroke capture, desktop control, network filtering, and process injection, while maintaining persistence through SYSTEM-leve...

items.title: From Endpoint to Funhouse: Changes in Ransomware Families and Kimsuky-Related Distribution Cases
items.description: A North Korean threat actor distributed Funhouse ransomware through malicious Korean-language documents disguised as resumes. Funhouse is a variant of the previously observed Endpoint ransomware. The attack chain involves multi-stage scripts including Batch, VBS, and PowerShell, leading to Quasar RAT installation before deploying the final ransomware payload. The campaign shares significant similarities with earlier Kimsuky Endpoint ransomware operations from early 2026, including identical mutex values, similar batch file structures, and comparable Quasar RAT configurations. The ransomware maintains key characteristics of the Endpoint family while updating encryption extensions, contact information, and C2 infrastructure. A notable shift involves using HWP documents instead of LNK files as initial infection vectors.

items.title: Inside a brand deal scam targeting YouTube creators
items.description: A sophisticated phishing campaign targets YouTube content creators through personalized sponsorship emails impersonating legitimate brands like Hollyland, Nike, and Spotify. Attackers send customized collaboration offers referencing specific videos from targets' channels, then direct them to fraudulent platforms that appear legitimate with campaign metrics and income calculators. The scheme culminates in a Google sign-in request that either captures credentials directly or requests excessive account permissions. Once compromised, attackers lock victims out by changing recovery methods and can misuse the account to spread scams to followers. The modular campaign operates globally, targeting creators in Peru, Japan, and English-speaking regions, using multiple domains while maintaining similar functionality and design patterns across variants.

items.title: Threat Overview: NetScaler Zero Days CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772 Being Exploited in Production Environments (Updated September 30)
items.description: Two critical zero-day vulnerabilities in NetScaler ADC and Gateway systems are being actively exploited in the wild. CVE-2026-88771 is a remote code execution vulnerability allowing unauthenticated command injection, while CVE-2026-88772 is a DTLS memory overflow flaw enabling RCE or DoS attacks. Threat actors deployed webshells through these vulnerabilities to establish initial access and persistence. The CVE-2026-88771 exploitation involves a three-stage command injection chain poisoning log files, while CVE-2026-88772 exploitation drops .deb webshell files. Attackers used PHP webshells with RC4 encryption for command and control communications, targeting custom directories within NetScaler Gateway interfaces. Cortex Xpanse identified over 50,000 potentially vulnerable exposed instances.

items.title: DNS as C2 in Noir, An AI-Developed Crypto Wallet Drainer
items.description: A cryptocurrency wallet-drainer kit called Noir uses DNS TXT records and DNS-over-HTTPS (DoH) as a dynamic command-and-control mechanism. The loader queries public DoH services to discover active infrastructure hosted on Cloudflare Pages, allowing operators to redirect deployed lures by changing a single DNS record. The drainer does not require victims to enter seed phrases or private keys; instead, it requests wallet connection permissions and obtains spending approvals that appear less suspicious than direct transfers. The architecture separates long-lived phishing lures from short-lived operational infrastructure, with 60-second DNS caching and self-healing retry logic. Extensive plain-English code comments suggest AI-assisted development, documenting bugs, fixes, and design decisions. The kit serves as a shared service across multiple cryptocurrency-themed phishing campaigns.

items.title: The Scalpel vs. The Sledgehammer: Lessons in Precision Triage from the .conf26 SOC
items.description: During a live Security Operations Center shift at .conf26 in Denver, analysts investigated Incident ES_00244 involving an exploit link detected by Cisco Secure Firewall. The challenge arose when 15 devices were found communicating with a single IP address (13.226.251.40) flagged for hosting malicious domains moonlighthathel[.]org and ukankingwithea[.]com. Investigation revealed the IP was an Amazon CloudFront CDN node simultaneously serving legitimate services including Samsung Health, Mindtickle learning platform, and Amazon Video. Using AI-assisted analysis, firewall logs, and packet forensics through Endace, analysts isolated one unmanaged Intel laptop generating malicious traffic among 14 benign connections. Instead of blocking the shared IP and disrupting legitimate services, analysts implemented precise DNS object blocks targeting only the malicious domains at the Cisco Firepower Threat Defense perimeter, successfully neutralizing the threat while maintaining normal operations for all other attendees.

items.title: Malicious Twitch Browser Extension Exposes 30,000 Users' OAuth Tokens to Russian Bot Service
items.description: A malicious browser extension called 'Twitch Enhanced Viewer | JeetBot' distributed on Chrome Web Store and Firefox Add-ons captures and forwards users' live Twitch OAuth session tokens to Russian-controlled proxy servers. The extension, with approximately 30,000 Chrome users and 552 Firefox users, markets itself as a quality-of-life tool for blocking ads and unlocking streams. While delivering these features, it secretly extracts users' account-scoped OAuth tokens and forwards them as query parameters to operator-controlled infrastructure. Current versions append tokens inline during video playlist redirects, while earlier builds explicitly POSTed tokens to dedicated collection endpoints. The operator is identified as a commercial Russian bot service called JeetBot, with infrastructure hosted across German and cloud providers.

items.title: KATARU: IoT Malware Adopts Public LPE Exploits
items.description: KATARU is an IoT malware variant discovered in August 2026 through Telnet credential brute-forcing against a honeypot from Vietnam. While maintaining traditional Mirai-style botnet capabilities, it distinguishes itself through an extensive feature set including multiple Linux local privilege escalation exploits, comprehensive persistence mechanisms across Linux and embedded platforms, encrypted C2 communications using X25519 and ChaCha20-Poly1305, anti-analysis techniques, and decoy traffic generation. Implementation artifacts strongly suggest AI-assisted development, evidenced by architecture-mismatched x86 shellcode in ARM binaries, RFC test vectors as configuration values, and untested cross-platform persistence logic. The malware attempts various privilege escalation paths through system misconfigurations and public exploits, establishes persistence across numerous startup mechanisms, and supports multiple DDoS attack vectors alongside SSH brute-forcing capabilities.

items.title: Artifactory Under Attack: In-the-Wild Exploitation of CVE-2026-42016, CVE-2026-42018 & CVE-2026-82329
items.description: Active exploitation of three critical vulnerabilities in JFrog Artifactory has been identified, with attackers chaining CVE-2026-42016, CVE-2026-42018, and CVE-2026-82329 to bypass authentication and gain administrative control. CVE-2026-42018 exposes internal anonymous-user tokens, CVE-2026-42016 enables privilege escalation through insufficient token validation, and CVE-2026-82329 allows unauthenticated access to administrative privileges. Post-exploitation activities include creating persistent administrator accounts, deploying malicious Groovy plugins for code execution, and installing Rust-based backdoors. Exploitation was observed between August 15 and September 8, 2026, affecting multiple organizations. Data indicates 67-69% of organizations running Artifactory had vulnerable instances at initial publication, with slow patching velocity for lower-severity CVEs despite active exploitation across environments.

items.title: Melofee: a look back at a Linux implant and its new variants
items.description: Three years after its initial discovery, the Melofee Linux implant has evolved with sophisticated new capabilities. The malware now features modularized architecture with hot-loadable components for shell functionality, file management, and command execution. New versions incorporate remote C2 infrastructure reconfiguration and enhanced stealth through a kernel rootkit based on the Reptile project. The implant uses RC4 encryption and supports multiple communication protocols including TCP, HTTP, HTTPS, and TLS. Analysis reveals two infrastructure clusters utilizing fake certificates impersonating Symantec and other entities. Code similarities establish links with Windows-targeting implants including CrowDoor, Hemigate, and RatelS, suggesting tool sharing among multiple Chinese state-linked threat groups. The modular design allows dynamic loading of up to eleven specialized modules via a common plugin interface.

items.title: Casbaneiro: A Banking Trojan with Distributed Data-Receiving Servers
items.description: In August 2026, a Casbaneiro campaign targeted Latin American users through phishing emails and PDFs themed as fake invoices and legal notices. The multi-stage infection chain includes HTA downloaders and AutoIt loaders, employing geofencing to filter victims by IP address location. The malware exhibits sophisticated evasion techniques, including distributed data-receiving servers, deliberate HTTP 403 responses, and activation only when victims access targeted banking websites. Casbaneiro steals email data, performs clipboard injection, and creates fake windows for fraudulent activities. The campaign specifically targets Argentina, Peru, Colombia, and Mexico while avoiding German, French, and English language systems. The malware splits stolen data across multiple servers and uses malformed HTTP packets to complicate detection and analysis efforts.

items.title: Threat Snapshot: Djinn Stealer
items.description: Djinn Stealer is a cross-platform information stealer delivered as a second-stage payload by the TaskWeaver Node.js loader. It employs a rules-based collection engine to harvest credentials and configuration data from cloud platforms, source control systems, package registries, infrastructure tooling, AI development assistants, browsers, SSH, and cryptocurrency wallets. The stolen data is archived, encrypted, and exfiltrated to attacker-controlled infrastructure. This threat has been observed following exploitation of the SimpleHelp vulnerability CVE-2026-48558. The stealer executes within a Node.js runtime context and communicates with command-and-control servers using encrypted channels for data exfiltration.

items.title: Mantax Otax: Indonesian Mobile Ransomware with Spyware Integration
items.description: A sophisticated mobile threat linked to Indonesian actors combines ransomware and spyware capabilities in a single attack vector. The malware is distributed via third-party file-sharing platforms through social engineering, targeting Android devices. It requests extensive permissions including device administrator, SMS, contacts, and accessibility access. The threat encrypts files using AES on Android 9 and earlier, appending .enc extensions, while stealing sensitive data including screen recordings, browser history, PINs, contacts, call logs, SMS messages, WhatsApp and Telegram chats. It establishes C2 communication via HTTPS and WebSockets using dynamic domain resolution through GitHub. Version 2 introduces UI hijacking, screen blocking, touch input interception, harassment features, and remote text-to-speech capabilities. The malware exfiltrates data through Firebase and Catbox services, enabling double-extortion through an interactive chat portal for ransom demands.

items.title: Mind the (Patch) Gap: Multiple Chinese Threat Actors Chain 0-day Exploits in Chrome & Windows
items.description: In September 2026, two Chinese threat actors, UTA0560 and JungleBamboo, were observed exploiting an identical Chrome zero-day vulnerability chain targeting NGOs and other organizations. The exploitation leveraged CVE-2026-85046 and CVE-2026-87491 in Chrome alongside CVE-2026-85880 in Windows kernel. These vulnerabilities had been patched in Chromium source code but not yet released to Chrome users, creating a patch-gap exploitation window. UTA0560 conducted spear-phishing campaigns using financial lures to deliver GRIMWEDGE JScript backdoor for reconnaissance and command execution. JungleBamboo employed generic phishing themes to deploy SUPERSTOMP loader, which installed the LONGTALE Chrome extension designed for credential theft, keylogging, and surveillance. Both actors used byte-for-byte identical shellcode, suggesting a shared exploit supply chain while deploying distinct post-exploitation tools tailored to their operational objectives.

items.title: Active exploitation of Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center vulnerabilities
items.description: Cisco Talos is tracking active exploitation of two vulnerabilities in Secure Firewall Management Center (FMC) Software. CVE-2026-20079 is a critical authentication bypass vulnerability allowing remote attackers to execute scripts and obtain root access. CVE-2026-20316 enables remote login using low-privileged accounts and can be chained with other vulnerabilities for privilege escalation. Three distinct threat actor clusters have been identified conducting post-compromise activities: UAT-12197 deployed web shells and credential theft tools; UAT-11823, overlapping with Russian APT Sandworm, deployed Cyclops Blink malware and established reverse shells; UAT-11988, a Qilin ransomware operator, conducted extensive reconnaissance, credential harvesting, and deployed ransomware after establishing persistent network access through tunneling tools. Customers are strongly advised to apply available hotfixes immediately.

items.title: Agents Gone Wild: An AI-Orchestrated Global Campaign Against PaperCut NG/MF
items.description: A likely Russian-speaking malicious cyber actor leveraged artificial intelligence to orchestrate a global campaign exploiting PaperCut NG/MF print management software via CVE-2026-81578 and CVE-2026-82078. Using AI agents powered by DeepSeek models and OpenAI's Codex, the adversary moved from empty workspace to first remote code execution in under four hours, compromising at least 440 PaperCut instances across 395 organizations in 48 countries. The campaign originated from IP 45.142.193.132, which had been tracked since July 2026 for attacks against various technologies. The adversary developed and tested exploits in a self-hosted lab environment before launching coordinated attacks using AI agents to achieve rapid compromise, with the fastest domain admin access achieved in just five minutes. Domain administrator access was confirmed in 12 organizations, primarily affecting educational institutions in the United States.

items.title: Warden Stealer: The Rapid Rise of an Infostealer with an Appetite for AI Agent Data
items.description: Warden Stealer is an emerging Rust-based infostealer-as-a-service that has rapidly become one of the most prevalent threats, distributed via malware-as-a-service model since August 2026. Unlike most competitors, it includes a dedicated loader and built-in cryptocurrency clipper. The malware targets over 200 cryptocurrency wallet extensions, 360+ applications across 13 categories, and is notably one of the first infostealers specifically collecting AI assistant and agentic coding tool data, including tokens, credentials, and prompt histories from Claude, Codex, Grok, and Cursor. Operating through tiered subscriptions ranging from $149 for three days to $1,500 monthly, Warden Stealer employs sophisticated obfuscation techniques, morphing capabilities, and bypasses Application-Bound Encryption to steal browser data. The malware avoids CIS and Baltic countries and is distributed through cracked software, game cheats, malvertising, and ClickFix campaigns.

items.title: Threat Actors Exploit Critical AhsayCBS Flaws to Drop Webshells and XMRig Cryptominer
items.description: Beginning October 7, 2026, threat actors exploited two critical vulnerabilities in AhsayCBS backup utility (CVE-2026-105133 and CVE-2026-105134) to achieve unauthenticated remote code execution on exposed systems. The attackers chained these vulnerabilities together, first bypassing authentication and then executing code with SYSTEM privileges. Post-exploitation activities included deploying JSP webshells, installing XMRig cryptocurrency miners disguised as Microsoft Edge processes, and dropping an AI-assisted PowerShell script that monitors and terminates Task Manager to hide mining operations. The attackers established persistence through a fake Windows service named MicrosoftEdgeUpdateSvc and utilized a vulnerable WinRing0x64.sys kernel driver to enable kernel-level hardware access for optimized mining performance. All AhsayCBS versions through 10.3.4 are affected, with managed service providers being the primary targets.

items.title: MATCHBOIL: New tricks, same old evil intentions
items.description: ESET researchers documented the evolution of MATCHBOIL, a custom C# downloader used by Russia-aligned APT group UAC-0099. The malware downloads payloads from command-and-control servers, installs them, and establishes persistence on victim machines. Development traces back to April 2024, with continuous improvements through April 2026. Early versions used Unicode symbol obfuscation and custom string encryption, while later iterations employed the Eziriz .NET Reactor obfuscator. UAC-0099 progressively added sandbox detection methods, modified persistence mechanisms from registry keys to scheduled tasks, and introduced deceptive graphical interfaces. All observed victims were Ukrainian organizations across transportation, manufacturing, and energy sectors. The group typically distributes MATCHBOIL through spearphishing emails containing malicious links that download VBScript files. MATCHBOIL often delivers MATCHWOK backdoor as its final payload.

items.title: US disrupts Chinese hacking tools as 7 govts warn of PRC spies stealing sensitive data worldwide
items.description: The FBI seized seven web domains linked to Integrity Technology Group, a Chinese security firm allegedly providing hacking tools to Beijing-backed operatives. These tools enabled attacks on critical infrastructure, including a South Carolina power company and universities in Taiwan. The Flax Typhoon group utilized a Mirai-based botnet from 2021 to infect internet-connected devices, scan networks, and launch cyberattacks while concealing Chinese government hackers' locations. The malicious activity involved vulnerability scanning via Microscan tool, cross-site scripting, password spraying on Microsoft Exchange servers, and data exfiltration using FishHub malware. A joint advisory from US, UK, Australia, Canada, Japan, New Zealand, and Spain warned that Chinese state-sponsored actors continue targeting organizations worldwide to steal sensitive information from critical infrastructure networks.

items.title: Suspected TraderTraitor Group Uses Trojanized Terraform Provider to Deliver Cross-Platform Malware
items.description: In July 2026, Zscaler ThreatLabz uncovered a sophisticated campaign utilizing a trojanized Terraform provider to deliver cross-platform malware targeting cryptocurrency and Web3 developers. The attack begins with a malicious Terraform provider that downloads a Bash loader from a HashiCorp-themed lookalike domain, which then selects and deploys payloads tailored to the victim's operating system (macOS, Linux, or Windows). Encrypted executables are concealed within fake font files and extracted using marker-based techniques and AES-256-CBC decryption. The campaign delivers FLATROOF, a Rust-based backdoor with platform-specific persistence mechanisms and multiple C2 channels including Telegram Bot API and GitHub. Python-based information stealers target browser credentials, cookies, cryptocurrency wallet extensions, and system information. The attack culminates with ROOFDECK backdoor deployment, featuring resilient C2 discovery through cryptographically signed Pastebin dead drops and Nostr profile metadata, p...

items.title: NEBULA: Seven Fake AI SDK Packages on npm Install a Windows RAT That Needs No DLL
items.description: In late September 2026, an actor deployed seven malicious npm packages masquerading as a NebulaAI software development kit to deliver a Windows remote-access trojan. The operation, tracked as NEBULA, spans four sequential burner accounts (nebulallms through nebulallms4), with api-nebula and llm-nebula remaining downloadable. Each package presents a convincing AI client facade while hiding an obfuscated installation hook executing malicious logic. The underlying RAT operates exclusively through direct NT and win32k syscalls, bypassing standard DLL imports with an empty Import Address Table. Features include hidden-desktop remote control (HVNC), Kernel Streaming for camera and microphone monitoring, and Winlogon Shell persistence. The payload is a customized KNTRAT variant communicating with 65.87.7.132 using user-agent kntrat/0xB15B00B6. The implant masquerades as conhost.exe and suppressed beaconing during analysis, consistent with embedded anti-analysis provisions.

items.title: Unknown Threat Actor Uses AI-Driven ARTEX to Target South Korean Finance
items.description: An unidentified threat actor, likely Chinese-speaking and financially motivated, conducted targeted attacks against South Korean financial institutions between late September and early October 2026, successfully exfiltrating data. The adversary utilized ARTEX, a Chinese-developed open-source agentic penetration testing tool, combined with large language models including DeepSeek v4.1-flash, GLM-5.3, and Grok 4.6. Analysis of exposed directories revealed Claude Code session histories, ARTEX configuration files, and operational details showing a two-server architecture involving Hong Kong-based infrastructure. The threat actor demonstrated sophisticated tradecraft by leveraging AI tooling to enhance operational tempo, enabling multiple intrusions within a compressed timeframe. Evidence suggests the attacker also researched Korean data breach marketplaces and Telegram channels for selling stolen information.

items.title: From Guest Complaints to Malware: Blockchain Abuse Targets Hotels
items.description: Threat actors are conducting email campaigns targeting the accommodation industry using fake guest complaints, reviews, and inquiries. These emails deliver malicious LNK shortcut files disguised as images, which ultimately deploy blockchain-abusing malware families known as EtherRAT and TONResolver. Both malware types resolve command and control infrastructure by querying public blockchain APIs (Ethereum and TON respectively) instead of using hardcoded domains. This technique allows operators to rotate infrastructure cheaply through small blockchain transactions while making traditional takedown efforts ineffective. The campaigns represent an evolution from earlier Booking.com-spoofing operations that used ClickFix fake CAPTCHAs to deliver remote access trojans. The threat actors likely employ generative AI to create unique email variants, making detection more challenging.

items.title: Bypassing the Gatekeepers: How a Global Phishing Campaign Turns Google's Infrastructure into a Trust Proxy
items.description: Cybercriminals are exploiting legitimate Google infrastructure in a sophisticated phishing operation that bypasses email security gateways and enterprise firewalls. The attack chains together six distinct Google properties including Meet, Search, DoubleClick, Custom Search, Tag Manager and Analytics to proxy malicious traffic through trusted domains. Victims' email addresses are encoded in URL fragments and stripped before server-side logging. Landing pages dynamically impersonate target organizations by pulling live logos from Clearbit, capturing real-time website screenshots, and validating domains via Google's DNS API. The operation includes multilingual support for 16 languages and dual execution tracks: credential harvesting with immediate Telegram exfiltration, or silent ScreenConnect remote access tool installation. Lures span document reviews, credential expiry notices, package delivery, payment notifications, government benefits and voicemail themes targeting manufacturing, government, finance and...

items.title: Redis Cryptomining Botnet Compromised 3,562 Servers, Exposed by the Operator's Own Files
items.description: An exposed directory at 188.245.99.156 revealed a comprehensive cryptomining toolkit containing 147 files including Python exploit source code, campaign logs, and Windows registry hives. Analysis confirms 3,562 Redis servers were compromised across two campaign runs targeting 12,966 hosts. The operation exploited unauthenticated Redis instances using rogue replication techniques to inject cron jobs that deployed XMRig miners. Victims spanned Redis versions 2.8.17 through 7.2.0 across outdated and current Linux distributions, indicating misconfiguration rather than version-specific vulnerabilities. The toolkit also targeted WordPress, MongoDB, and SSH but achieved zero confirmed compromises through those vectors. A separate February 2026 open directory linked by wallet reuse revealed Meterpreter deployment capabilities, extending the operator's known activity timeline by five months. The operation mined Monero through pool.moneroocean.stream with the same wallet used on the operator's own Windows-based work...

items.title: Inside a Packed Android RAT Loader
items.description: Hagaseca is an Android malware cluster linked to exposed Android Debug Bridge (ADB) services, focusing on the THost9 RAT loader variant. The malware conceals executable code within an APK that loads tc9.dex, a stage providing shell access, file transfer, and ADB propagation capabilities. Public incidents connect THost4 and THost9 to exposed Android and Redroid systems from October 2024 through 2026. The loader uses XOR and gzip packing, establishes persistence through foreground services, exploits accessibility features for device control, and downloads additional stages from test.hagaseca.com. The tc9.dex stage implements remote administration, discovers ADB endpoints via mDNS, scans entire /16 networks, authenticates with prepared keys, and installs itself on vulnerable systems. The malware exhibits worm-like behavior, spreading opportunistically through unsecured ADB services exposed to the internet, particularly affecting Redroid container deployments and devices with public ADB over Wi-Fi.

items.title: Canto incognito: tracking the PoeLLM malware
items.description: Since April 2026, PoeLLM malware has been actively targeting exposed AI/LLM and open-source services including LiteLLM, Ollama, Gotenberg, and Gitea, with possible Ivanti Sentry targeting. The campaign employs an unusual command-and-control mechanism where infected systems derive C2 server addresses from keywords embedded in a poem hosted on GitHub. This financially-motivated operation deploys XMRig and Iron cryptocurrency miners, connecting victims to Kryptex mining infrastructure. Compromised hosts are repurposed as scanners and exploit servers to expand the botnet, which has impacted over 3,400 victim servers with peak activity exceeding 800 active servers daily. The campaign appears linked to an Italian-speaking threat actor and predominantly affects victims in the United States and Western Europe. Vulnerable routers are exploited to serve as C2 infrastructure.

items.title: The state of AI-analysis evasion in malware
items.description: Malware authors are developing techniques to obstruct automated AI analysis by embedding natural-language instructions within their code. This 'AI-analysis evasion' targets the pipeline that extracts text from samples and submits it to language models for triage or classification. Analysis of 84 samples across four malware families (FRUITSHELL, PLOTSAFE, HOLLOWCLAD, and MANTLEMAZE) from January 2025 through July 2026 reveals progression from simple comments claiming benign functionality to template spraying across multiple LLM formats and intimidation tactics invoking copyright, government contracts, and security certifications. The cheapest technique—direct instructions to ignore samples—proved most effective, steering outcomes favorably for attackers in approximately 35% of test runs. However, these techniques must remain in plaintext, making them consistently detectable. The fundamental defense requires treating extracted text as evidence rather than instruction, ensuring analysis pipelines maintain exp...

items.title: ClearFake WebDAV infection chain delivers Amatera stealer, ZigCryptoStealer, and NetSupport Manager
items.description: An investigation revealed a sophisticated cryptocurrency and credential-stealing operation using Amatera stealer as the primary payload. The attack chain leverages Cloudflare Workers to inject JavaScript stored on BNB Smart Chain, presenting fake Google CAPTCHA prompts that lead to WebDAV-based DLL execution. Two parallel infection chains were identified, one loading through a DLL named 'pf.ch' and another through 'verification.google', both delivering Amatera stealer with different secondary payloads. The 'pf.ch' variant deployed ZigCryptoStealer via NativeAOT loader and a Go-based reverse proxy, while the 'verification.google' variant installed NetSupport Manager with C2 infrastructure in Russia. The operation affects numerous countries with primary focus on stealing cryptocurrency wallets, credentials from password managers, and various authentication data through extensive collection rules targeting over 400 applications.

items.title: Phishing Campaign Abuses Microsoft Power BI to Deploy Rogue RMMs
items.description: In September, a phishing campaign exploited legitimate Microsoft Power BI domains to distribute rogue ScreenConnect remote monitoring tools. Attackers sent phishing emails with embedded links redirecting victims to fake reference documents hosted on Power BI infrastructure. Clicking 'Download Reference' opened attacker-controlled websites that fingerprinted victims' systems and browsers before triggering malicious ScreenConnect installer downloads. The attack deployed multiple ScreenConnect instances for persistent remote access, with the second client connected to attacker infrastructure. Following deployment, threat actors executed defense evasion tools and created scheduled tasks running persistence scripts every two minutes. The campaign used browser fingerprinting and Telegram bots to filter victims and track infections, while abusing trusted Microsoft domains to bypass email security controls and increase attack credibility.

items.title: FortiBleed Operations Continue Targeting Exposed Systems Leading to Reports of Lockouts
items.description: FortiBleed is an active global credential-compromise campaign targeting internet-facing Fortinet FortiGate firewalls and SSL VPN gateways, with over 86,644 compromised devices verified across 194 countries. The campaign exploits reused or leaked credentials and legacy SHA-256 password storage, enabling threat actors to harvest and crack authentication data at scale using distributed GPU clusters. Attackers scan for exposed FortiGate SSL VPN portals, collect credentials through stuffing and password spraying, and crack stolen password hashes offline. Once access is gained, they create new administrative accounts for persistence and conduct Active Directory enumeration to expand access. Affected organizations may experience lockouts as threat actors delete or modify existing accounts. The operation functions as an initial-access broker, with connections observed to INC/Lynx and Payload ransomware affiliates, representing a significant threat requiring immediate defensive action.

items.title: 16 Malicious Firefox Extensions Steal Cryptocurrency Wallet Credentials
items.description: A coordinated campaign of 16 malicious Firefox extensions has been identified targeting cryptocurrency wallet users. The extensions masquerade as wallet portals, desktop utilities, and browser tools while intercepting recovery phrases and private keys during wallet import flows. Four large extensions clone Rabby Wallet (misspelled as Raabby WaIIet), while twelve smaller extensions impersonate OKX Wallet. All variants capture 12- or 24-word mnemonics and private keys, transmitting stolen credentials to attacker-controlled Cloudflare Workers endpoints. Fifteen extensions communicate with icy-star-f45c.workers.dev infrastructure. The campaign reuses code markers, network infrastructure, and credential-handling logic, indicating connection to crypto-theft operations identified in August 2026. Mozilla has unpublished these extensions. Users who entered credentials should immediately create new wallets and transfer assets.

items.title: DarkSword/Coruna Open Directory Finding
items.description: Five hosts exposed the complete DarkSword/Coruna iOS exploitation platform through open directories, revealing an active commercial exploitation-as-a-service operation. The platform targets cryptocurrency wallets across 18 different applications, extracting BIP39 recovery phrases and conducting automated theft. Analysis of the production server recovered 11 victim recovery phrases, 179 device loot directories, and a 75-account control-plane roster indicating an agent/reseller model. A separate China-based operator is deploying identical tooling through independent infrastructure at 66ds[.]lol, representing a distinct threat actor from previously documented DarkSword users. The infrastructure was operationally active during analysis, with beacon telemetry showing Chinese iOS devices polling every three seconds for hours. Development work targeting iOS 26 via CVE-2026-31001 was discovered but remains undeployed.

items.title: Inside PhantomPolia: Remus Stealer Delivery via Donut Shellcode in ClickFix Campaign
items.description: LevelBlue observed a ClickFix campaign delivering Remus Stealer through compromised websites using PhantomPolia, a JavaScript loader that retrieves encrypted configurations from Ethereum Sepolia smart contracts via public RPC endpoints. The loader decrypts configurations locally using PBKDF2 and AES-GCM to obtain C2 domains. Victims are tricked into executing PowerShell commands that retrieve and decrypt additional configurations using AES-CBC before downloading bundled installers containing AutoIt executables. The AutoIt script decrypts embedded Donut-packed shellcode and executes it from allocated memory, ultimately loading Remus Stealer. This information-stealing malware collects system data, credentials, browser information, password managers, and cryptocurrency wallets. Stolen data is compressed using custom methods and encrypted with ChaCha20 before exfiltration to attacker-controlled servers.

items.title: TensorLake npm SDK Compromised in ChainDrop Shai-Hulud Credential-Stealing Attack
items.description: The Tensorlake npm SDK version 0.5.144 was compromised in a ChainDrop/Shai-Hulud supply chain attack, affecting a package with approximately 12,000 weekly downloads. The malicious release contains obfuscated code that harvests credentials from multiple sources including npm tokens, GitHub tokens, AWS credentials, HashiCorp Vault, Kubernetes configurations, SSH keys, and AI development tools. A preinstall hook executes the payload during installation, establishing persistence through scheduled tasks and supporting remote code execution. The attack uses an Ethereum contract to resolve command-and-control endpoints and implements a dead-man switch that monitors stolen GitHub tokens, triggering destructive actions if revoked. The malicious code can self-propagate by republishing compromised versions to other packages associated with the victim's publishing identity, extending the worm's reach across the npm ecosystem.

items.title: RMM Tools Being Distributed Through Phishing Attacks (ScreenConnect, FleetDeck, Datto, SimpleHelp, JumpCloud, N-able)
items.description: Multiple Remote Monitoring and Management (RMM) tools are being distributed through phishing campaigns involving video files and email attachments. Threat actors exploit legitimate RMM solutions like ScreenConnect, FleetDeck, Datto, SimpleHelp, JumpCloud, and N-able to gain remote access to compromised systems while evading security detection. These tools, typically used for legitimate IT administration purposes, are weaponized through various delivery methods including LNK files, BAT scripts, VBS files, and PDF documents disguised as business documents. The campaigns leverage social engineering tactics, presenting fake Adobe Acrobat updates, DocuSign viewers, and document access prompts to trick victims into installing these remote access tools. Each RMM tool contains configuration data linking back to attacker infrastructure, including deployment IDs, account identifiers, and command-and-control server addresses embedded within installation files.

items.title: StyleSmuggler: Magento and Adobe Commerce 0-day RCE under active attack
items.description: An unpatched zero-day vulnerability dubbed StyleSmuggler affects all current versions of Magento and Adobe Commerce, including 2.4.9, enabling unauthenticated remote code execution. Active exploitation began on September 4th, 2026. The attack operates in two stages: injecting malicious PHP code into Magento's template system using styles properties to evade safeguards, then executing the poisoned code via failed payment emails. Upon successful compromise, attackers deploy a Rust-based backdoor disguised as legitimate system processes (kworker, fc-cache, or chronyd) that connects to command and control servers. The backdoor uses NTP-shaped UDP traffic for C2 communication to evade detection. A second unrelated attacker has also been observed exploiting the same vulnerability to deploy PHP web shells. Affected merchants should deploy immediate mitigation measures, scan for compromise, and temporarily disable GraphQL until an official patch is released.

items.title: Tracking BigBear 2.0 Evilginx2 Phishing Campaign
items.description: In June 2026, researchers uncovered BigBear 2.0, a rebranded Evilginx2-based phishing-as-a-service framework targeting Microsoft 365 credentials globally. The operation, managed by operator 'General Boss', deployed 42 VPS nodes primarily hosted on Vultr infrastructure, utilizing the 'offy' phishlet configuration. The platform employed adversary-in-the-middle techniques with geo-matched residential proxy pools across 69 countries, real-time Telegram exfiltration, and automated cookie replay to bypass MFA. The campaign exfiltrated 5,137 credential records including 474 complete MFA-bypassed authentications, 1,032 plaintext passwords, and 4,148 session cookies, affecting 3,331 unique victim IPs across 40+ countries. The multi-user PhaaS panel was leased to at least five identified affiliate operators. Custom JavaScript injections disabled FIDO2/WebAuthn MFA while residential proxies bypassed anti-bot detection, enabling persistent access to compromised Microsoft 365 environments.

items.title: Behind the Connect Button: The Fake AI Ads Campaign
items.description: Security researchers uncovered a sophisticated human-operated phishing platform disguising itself as AI advertising products for major platforms including Muse, Gemini, Claude, ChatGPT, and Perplexity. The campaign uses a Browser-in-the-Browser technique, creating fake authentication windows that appear legitimate while remaining on phishing domains. When victims click 'Connect' buttons, operators intercept credentials and MFA challenges in real-time through a state machine that can retry passwords and adapt to different authentication methods. The platform targets advertising account managers and recruiters, with infrastructure built on Next.js and Socket.IO, reusing the same codebase across multiple brand impersonations. The operation extends beyond AI products to include refund scams and fake recruitment sites, all connected through shared backend infrastructure on Railway and Render hosting services.
